items.headline: Stocks making biggest moves midday: Hindustan Copper, Vedanta, Vodafone Idea, Blue Star and more
items.body: Indian equities were under pressure in midday trade, with benchmarks slipping despite pockets of sharp stock-specific action. The Nifty was hovering around the 25,250 mark, marginally down, while the Sensex was trading near 82,000, lower by roughly the same margin. Select consumer durables stocks moved higher, metal counters cracked after a brutal reversal, telecom saw aggressive buying, and railway-linked names stayed in focus ahead of the Union Budget. Here are the top movers and shakers at this hour: Hindustan Copper Hindustan Copper share price fell about 9% by midday after global copper prices turned volatile and exchanges raised margin requirements, triggering heavy profit booking. The stock reversed sharply after hitting an upper circuit in the previous session. According to market reports, CME raised margin requirements on copper trades after prices surged to record highs, forcing leveraged positions to unwind. The sell-off came despite copper remaining strong in both domestic and international markets. Copper prices have climbed sharply in recent months, driven by demand from power grids, electric vehicles, renewable energy installations and data centres. Hindustan Copper, which has emerged as a direct proxy to the metal’s rally, has seen outsized gains over the past year, making it vulnerable when sentiment turns even briefly cautious. Vedanta Vedanta share price slipped over 8% by midday after metal stocks came under broad selling pressure despite strong December quarter earnings. The stock tracked the sharp fall across the metal pack, where recent outperformers saw aggressive selling. Vedanta had reported a 60% year-on-year jump in consolidated profit for the December quarter, supported by higher base metal prices and record output in key segments. Revenue also rose strongly, and management flagged the quarter as a milestone in terms of operating performance. Vodafone Idea Vodafone Idea share price rose about 10% by midday after the company said it plans to invest Rs 45,000 crore over the next three years to return to a growth path. The debt-laden telecom operator said the investment will be directed towards aggressive network expansion, conversion of 2G sites and strengthening 4G and 5G coverage across priority circles. Management said the capital expenditure plan is in addition to investments already made over the past six quarters. In its December quarter update, Vodafone Idea reported a narrower net loss and a rise in average revenue per user, aided by customer upgrades. The company also highlighted recent fund-raising efforts and government relief measures related to adjusted gross revenue dues, which it said mark an inflection point for the business. Metal stocks Metal stocks declined sharply by midday after extreme price swings in global markets led to widespread profit booking. The Nifty Metal index was trading about 4.5% lower by midday, with selling pressure visible across most constituents. Hindustan Zinc was down nearly 9%, while NALCO declined over 8% and Hindalco Industries slipped close to 6%. Copper prices, while still strong on a longer-term view, have seen sharp intraday moves. ALSO READSilver, Gold ETFs plunge 12%: Wall Street experts warn of as much as 50% crash ahead Railway stocks Railway stocks showed mixed movement by midday as budget expectations kept the sector in focus. Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers rose about 7% after reporting strong December quarter numbers, with revenue and profit posting sharp year-on-year growth. Titagarh Rail Systems gained around 1.5%, while RVNL and Jupiter Wagons slipped modestly amid broader market weakness. Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation traded marginally higher. The Economic Survey noted steady freight momentum and underlined the role of railways in supporting industrial activity, keeping attention firmly on the sector ahead of the Union Budget. MTAR Technologies MTAR Technologies share price rose nearly 8% by midday after the company reported a sharp jump in December quarter profit. The precision engineering firm said profit more than doubled year-on-year, supported by execution across clean energy, space and defence segments. Revenue growth and improved margins added to positive sentiment, with the stock touching a fresh high earlier in the session before paring some gains. ALSO READForget Large cap IT: Check Nuvama’s top 3 midcap IT picks with up to 49% upside potential Dixon Technologies Dixon Technologies share price was marginally lower by midday after the company flagged softer smartphone shipments in the post-festive quarter. The electronics manufacturer said revenue from its mobile and EMS division declined due to high inventory levels and rising memory costs, which weighed on volumes. Management indicated that demand conditions remain watchful as the industry adjusts after a strong festive season. Blue Star Blue Star share price rose nearly 4% by midday after the company said it expects a strong March quarter for its room air conditioner business. The country’s leading air-conditioner maker said demand momentum is improving after a challenging first three quarters of the year. In an investor presentation, the company flagged plans to raise room AC prices in the fourth quarter to offset rupee depreciation and higher commodity costs. Blue Star said dealer network expansion is progressing as planned and inventory levels have normalised following the energy-label change effective January 1, 2026. For the December quarter, revenue rose 4% year-on-year to Rs 2,925 crore, while net profit declined 39% to Rs 81 crore due to cost pressures. Operating performance remained stable, with EBITDA rising 5% and margins improving slightly. Management said order bookings in commercial air conditioning remain healthy and demand from factories and data centres continues to provide support.
items.snippet: Metal stocks cracked after a sharp global reversal, Vodafone Idea surged on a ₹45,000-crore investment plan, while railway shares stayed in focus ahead of the Union Budget as benchmarks slipped at midday.

items.headline: This simple aluminum foil idea may help deter dogs and cats from furniture without expensive training prod
items.body: How aluminum foil may help keep dogs and cats off furniture? Many pet owners know the feeling. You leave the room for a few minutes and return to find your dog stretched across the couch or your cat curled up on your favorite chair. While comfortable furniture naturally attracts pets, not every family wants to share every seat. That is why a simple aluminum foil trick continues to attract attention among dog and cat owners. It is affordable, easy to try, and requires no special equipment. More importantly, it focuses on changing a pet's choice rather than using punishment.The idea is simple. Place a sheet of aluminum foil over the area where your pet usually jumps. Some pets hesitate because the surface feels unfamiliar and makes a crinkling sound under their paws. Others may not react at all. That difference is completely normal. Every dog and every cat has its own personality, confidence level, and learning style. Instead of treating aluminum foil as a guaranteed solution, experienced trainers view it as one possible tool that can support positive behavior.The real goal is not to scare a pet away from furniture. The goal is to guide the pet toward a place where it is welcome to rest. When combined with patience and rewards, this simple household item may help some families create new habits without spending money on commercial deterrent products.Why do some pets hesitate when they step on aluminum foil?Animals experience the world differently than people do. Dogs and cats rely heavily on touch, sound, and curiosity while exploring their surroundings. A smooth sofa feels familiar. A noisy sheet of aluminum foil does not. That unexpected change is often enough to make some pets pause before climbing onto furniture.132416539For many cats, the unusual texture beneath their paws is the biggest surprise. Cats generally prefer stable and predictable surfaces. When something suddenly crinkles or shifts slightly under their weight, they often decide to move somewhere else instead. Dogs can react in a similar way, although many larger or more confident dogs quickly investigate the new surface without concern.ALSO READ: Your dog knows the clocks changed, even if they can’t tell time —and what happens inside their brain is truly fascinatingThis is why reactions vary from one pet to another. Age, previous experiences, confidence, and even daily mood can influence how an animal responds. Owners should avoid assuming that the trick will work immediately or permanently. Watching the pet's behavior calmly provides better information than expecting identical results from every animal.Can aluminum foil become part of positive pet training?The most effective training always teaches pets what they should do instead of only showing them what they should avoid. If your dog walks away from the foil and chooses its own bed, reward that decision. If your cat climbs onto a nearby perch instead of the couch, offer praise, playtime, or another positive experience.132416547Pets learn through repetition. When the same good choice brings the same positive result, they begin to repeat that behavior naturally. Over time, the reward becomes more valuable than the furniture itself. That creates habits that continue even after the aluminum foil is removed.ALSO READ: The strange dog behavior called cobbing and what it says about your pet, according to animal behavior expertsPatience is just as important as the training method. Some pets understand new boundaries within days, while others need several weeks of consistent guidance. Rushing the process or becoming frustrated often slows progress. Calm repetition usually produces better long-term results than quick corrections.What should pet owners do if the aluminum foil trick does not work?Not every dog or cat will be bothered by aluminum foil. Some pets step across it without hesitation, while others lose interest after only a few encounters. That does not mean training has failed. It simply means your pet responds better to a different approach. Successful pet training has always depended on understanding the individual animal rather than expecting one solution to fit every home.Instead of continuing with a method that produces no change, focus on making approved resting areas more attractive. A comfortable pet bed placed near family activity often appeals to dogs. Cats usually enjoy elevated spaces where they can safely observe the room. Giving pets a place they truly enjoy often reduces the desire to climb onto furniture naturally.Daily routines also shape behavior. Pets that receive regular exercise, interactive play, and mental stimulation are less likely to search for entertainment by exploring places they should avoid. A tired dog often prefers its own bed after a long walk. A cat that has spent time climbing, chasing toys, or solving food puzzles is more likely to settle in its favorite perch instead of the couch.How can owners create lasting furniture rules?Consistency is the foundation of every successful training plan. Pets learn through repeated experiences. If they are allowed on the sofa one evening but corrected the next morning, they receive mixed messages that make learning much more difficult. Everyone in the household should follow the same rules so the pet receives clear and predictable guidance.The environment also plays an important role. If a pet always chooses one particular chair because it sits beside a sunny window or near family members, creating a similar resting place nearby may encourage better choices without conflict. Often, pets are looking for comfort, warmth, or companionship rather than the furniture itself.Positive reinforcement remains one of the most reliable ways to encourage lasting behavior. Calm praise, gentle attention, favorite treats, or a short play session immediately after a pet chooses its own resting spot helps strengthen that decision. As the habit grows stronger, rewards can gradually become less frequent while the behavior continues.Is this simple household trick worth trying?For many households, aluminum foil is an inexpensive experiment that carries very little risk when used properly. Because most people already keep it in the kitchen, there is no need to purchase special training products before seeing whether a pet responds to the unfamiliar surface.The important thing to remember is that aluminum foil is not the lesson. Good habits are the lesson. The foil simply gives some pets a reason to pause long enough for owners to redirect them toward a better choice. Once that new choice becomes part of the daily routine, the temporary aid is no longer needed.Every pet learns at its own pace. Some respond quickly, while others require more time and encouragement. By combining patience, clear boundaries, comfortable alternatives, and consistent rewards, owners create an environment where good behavior becomes natural. That approach protects furniture while strengthening trust between pets and the people who care for them.
items.snippet: A sheet of ordinary aluminum foil may discourage many dogs and cats from jumping onto sofas, counters, and tables because of its unusual texture and sound. While it isn't a guaranteed solution for every pet, experts say this inexpensive trick can be a useful part of gentle, reward-based furniture training.

items.headline: It’s an idea whose time has come: Oil Ministry on higher ethanol blending
items.body: The West Asia conflict has helped crystallise the government’s push towards higher ethanol blending in petrol in a bid to reduce crude oil import dependence with the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG) emphasising that it is an idea whose time has come. Currently, around one-third of India’s crude oil imports, which transit the Strait of Hormuz (SoH), are severely impacted. The government has managed to bring down dependence on SoH from over 50 per cent of its total crude imports in January and February to roughly 30 per cent by March. On higher ethanol blending with petrol, MoPNG Joint Secretary Sujata Sharma said, “The question was whether we are going to increase the base fuel. I must say that it is an idea whose time has arrived. By blending, we are saving on our imports. The stakeholder consultations are going on. In due course, we will inform you about it.” On flex fuel vehicles, she said, “The government is trying to bring all the stakeholders together. On one side, the automobile companies have to keep the vehicles ready and at the same time, our oil marketing companies also have to be ready to supply that kind of fuel. That exercise is going on. It’s more of a stakeholder consultation in bringing different stakeholders on a common platform.” Currently, 20 per cent ethanol is blended with petrol, which the government aims to increase further. Committed to biofuels Last week, the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) Additional Secretary Hanif Qureshi said that government is committed to use biofuels as far as possible and E20 has already taken place. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has already said that +/- 1 per cent blending can be there. So, about 21 per cent that much level can be there. The ethanol blended petrol (EBP) programme has helped India save roughly 6 million tonnes (mt), or around 44 million barrels annually. In the last 10 years, the programme has helped over 18 mt of crude oil imports, saving Rs 1.36 lakh crore in foreign exchange. On Tuesday, Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari emphasised that India should aspire to achieve 100 per cent ethanol blending in the near future, as vulnerabilities in oil exports amid the West Asia crisis have made it necessary for the country to become self-reliant in the energy sector. Published on April 22, 2026
items.snippet: India aims to increase ethanol blending in petrol beyond 20% to reduce crude oil imports and enhance energy self-reliance.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea shares: Emkay doubles Vi target price, upgrades stock from &#039;Sell&#039; rating
items.body: Emkay Global has upgraded Vodafone Idea Ltd (Vi) to &#039;Add&#039; rating from &#039;Sell&#039;, doubling its target price on the telecom stock to Rs 12 from Rs 6 earlier.  The domestic brokerage said the government has approved a major moratorium for Vi’s AGR liabilities, with minimal annual payments until FY35. It expects the development to provide significant cash flow relief and a turnaround opportunity for Vi.  &quot;The relief reduces the net present value (NPV) of the burden by 60–80 per cent, easing immediate survival pressure, along with the possibility of further reduction on reassessment of AGR dues,&quot; Emkay Global said.  Besides, Emkay Global said the move will enable Vodafone Idea to access bank funding for 4G and 5G expansion, helping the company arrest subscriber churn and market-share loss.  With the government freezing AGR dues, the NPV of the AGR dues has dropped to Rs 50,000 crore against Rs 87,000 crore earlier, with a further scope for reduction in liabilities in case of a favorable outcome of recalculation and reconciliation.  While the long-term sustainability of Vodafone Idea is no more a concern, Emkay said it will have to execute well to gain subscriber market share and migrate the subscriber base from 2G to 4G5G.  &quot;The stock trades at 12.5 times11.5 times FY27FY28 EVEbitda. While we maintain our target multiple at 12 times on Q3FY28E Ebitda, the reduction in the AGR debt and corresponding increase in Ebitda estimates leads to an increase in our TP to Rs 12 (from Rs 6). We upgrade the stock to ADD from Sell, considering the improved outlook for the company,&quot; it said.  &quot;We raise the target to Rs 12 (from Rs 6). Key risks: Inability to i) increase subscriber market share; ii) significantly increase ARPU with tariff repair, and iii) upgrade the subscriber base from 2G to 4G5G,&quot; it said.  Vi has earmarked Rs 45,000 crore of network capex over the next three years, targeting 4G expansion and 5G rollout across priority circles. Emkay said this will help VI increase its average revenue per user (ARPU) at a faster clip versus competition, considering it has a lower proportion of subscriber base on the 4G5G network.  &quot;Continued migration to data, rising usage, and tariff repair provide scope for ARPU-led Ebitda expansion, in our view, even without aggressive subscriber additions. Factoring in these changes, we raise our FY27FY28 revenue by 5 per cent4.9 per cent and Ebitda by 5.4 per cent4.2 per cent,&quot; Emkay said.
items.snippet: The domestic brokerage said the government has approved a major moratorium for Vis AGR liabilities with minimal annual payments until FY35 It expects the development to provide significant cash flow relief and a turnaround opportunity for Vi

items.headline: Spy chief Ajit Doval blends into crowd at Kerala eatery. Even owner ‘had no idea’ who he was
items.body: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval visited Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram on January 22 and 23. But unlike the usual official visits, this time there were no police sirens. There were no announcements. Most people did not even know that India’s most powerful security official was in the state. During his visit, Doval went to the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, where he help private meetings with scientists. Hardly anyone noticed him. For someone who works on India’s safety and security, being secretive is normal. But what made this visit special was how he maintained a low profile while touring the state. ALSO READ‘Won’t be bullied…willing to wait out Trump’s term’: How Ajit Doval’s bold ultimatum helped reset US trade talks One morning, around 8 AM, Doval walked into Maha Chips, a small and well-known snack shop near East Fort. During the Sabarimala season, the shop opens early, but at that time there are usually very few people. ALSO READ50 CCTV cameras crack, local sources: How Delhi police cracked iPhone snatching case of US national in 4 days A video that came out later showed him walking in with security guards wearing normal clothes. He looked around, bought some chips, and left calmly. Maha chips staff' response No one stared at him. No one whispered. No one stopped him. It was just like any other customer buying snacks in the morning. That is what made it interesting, one of the most powerful security officials in the country doing something very simple. Later, the staff at Maha Chips told Asianet News that they had no idea who he was. They only realised it after checking their CCTV footage. They said he behaved just like a regular person. Why did Doval visit Thiruvananthapuram? He came to look into problems with India’s space rockets. Recently, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), which is usually very reliable, had failed more than once. This worried the government a lot. Following instructions from Prime Minister Modi, Doval visited the space centre at Thumba. There, he spoke to senior scientists from the Indian Space Research Organisation. He wanted to understand what went wrong. The failures had happened at the same part of the rocket flight, called the third stage, which is very important. Because it happened again and again, the government wanted to be sure there was no danger to the country and no sabotage As a member of the Space Commission, Doval checked whether the problem was caused by any outside threat or internal issue. His focus was on learning the facts, not blaming anyone. After returning to New Delhi, he submitted a detailed report. The investigation found that there was no sabotage. However, it did point out some mistakes and areas that need fixing.
items.snippet: Ajit Doval’s quiet Thiruvananthapuram visit before PM Modi’s trip included a VSSC review of PSLV failures and an unexpected stop at a local chips shop.

items.headline: Quote of the day by Napoleon Hill, 'More gold has been mined from the thoughts of men than has been taken
items.body: Quote of the day by Napoleon Hill, More gold has been mined from the thoughts of men than has been taken from the earth , reminds us that the greatest riches are not always buried underground. Instead, they are found within the human mind—in the form of ideas, creativity, imagination, determination, and innovation. Every invention, successful business, scientific breakthrough, and artistic masterpiece began as a simple thought before becoming something that changed lives. Hill's quote teaches that our greatest asset is not what we own but what we are capable of imagining and creating.The central meaning of the quote is that ideas possess extraordinary value. Gold is limited because nature produces only a certain amount of it. Human creativity, however, has no such limits. Every day, people develop new solutions to old problems, invent technologies, improve businesses, and create works of art that inspire millions. A single idea can generate opportunities, improve communities, and even transform entire industries. This reminds us that the human mind is one of the world's most valuable resources.Important Life LessonOne of the most important lessons in the quote is the power of imagination. Every significant achievement once existed only in someone's thoughts. Airplanes, smartphones, life-saving medicines, renewable energy technologies, and countless everyday conveniences all started as ideas that many people initially considered impossible. Visionaries dared to imagine a better future and worked patiently to bring those ideas to life. Their success demonstrates that imagination is often the first step toward meaningful progress.132414241The quote also emphasizes the importance of believing in your own potential. Many people underestimate their abilities because they compare themselves with others or fear failure. Yet every person possesses unique experiences, talents, and perspectives that can lead to valuable ideas. Innovation does not belong exclusively to famous inventors or entrepreneurs. Teachers create better ways to educate students. Nurses improve patient care. Artists inspire emotions through creativity. Small business owners develop solutions that strengthen local communities. Every individual has the potential to contribute something meaningful.Quote of the Day HighlightsAnother valuable lesson is that knowledge becomes truly powerful when combined with action. Having a brilliant idea alone is not enough. Successful individuals transform thoughts into reality through planning, persistence, and consistent effort. Napoleon Hill consistently emphasized that success comes from organized action rather than wishful thinking. Many great opportunities remain unrealized simply because people hesitate to take the first step. Ideas achieve value only when they are developed, tested, improved, and shared with the world.The quote also highlights the importance of lifelong learning. The human mind grows stronger through curiosity and continuous education. Reading books, learning new skills, asking thoughtful questions, and exploring different perspectives expand creative thinking. Every new piece of knowledge has the potential to connect with existing ideas and generate innovative solutions. Individuals who remain curious throughout life often discover opportunities that others overlook because they continue challenging themselves to grow.Another important message is that setbacks should not discourage creative thinking. Many successful inventors, business leaders, and innovators experienced repeated failures before achieving lasting success. Failure often provides valuable information rather than permanent defeat. Each unsuccessful attempt teaches lessons that improve future efforts. The willingness to learn from mistakes transforms obstacles into stepping stones toward better ideas and stronger solutions.Phrase of the DayThe quote is especially meaningful in today's knowledge-driven economy. While natural resources remain valuable, many of the world's most influential companies have built their success primarily on innovation and intellectual creativity. Advances in technology, healthcare, education, engineering, and communication continue to demonstrate that human ideas generate enormous economic and social value. This reinforces Hill's belief that creative thinking often produces greater wealth than physical resources alone.Another important lesson is the value of collaboration. Some of history's greatest achievements emerged from teams of people sharing ideas rather than individuals working alone. Diverse perspectives often produce stronger solutions because each person contributes unique knowledge and experiences. Respectful discussion, open-mindedness, and teamwork encourage innovation by combining different ways of thinking into something greater than any one individual could accomplish independently.Valuable TeachingsThe quote also teaches personal responsibility. Since every person possesses the ability to think creatively, each individual has the responsibility to develop that gift. Instead of waiting for opportunities to appear, people can create opportunities through problem-solving, initiative, and perseverance. Developing strong habits such as reading, critical thinking, goal-setting, and continuous improvement allows ideas to flourish over time.Another valuable insight is that true wealth extends beyond money. While creative ideas often generate financial success, they also produce benefits that cannot be measured in dollars alone. A teacher's innovative lesson may inspire future scientists. A doctor's research may save lives. A community volunteer's creative project may strengthen neighborhoods. A parent's wisdom may shape future generations. The richest ideas are those that improve both individual lives and society as a whole.Ultimately, Napoleon Hill's quote encourages people to recognize the unlimited potential of the human mind. Unlike material resources, creativity becomes stronger the more it is used. Every challenge presents an opportunity for innovation. Every question invites discovery. Every dream begins with a thought. The greatest treasures waiting to be discovered may already exist within the imagination of ordinary people willing to think boldly and act with determination.
items.snippet: Quote of the day by Napoleon Hill is a timeless reminder that ideas are among humanity's greatest resources. Creative thinking, lifelong learning, perseverance, and purposeful action have transformed civilizations and continue to shape the future. By believing in our potential, nurturing curiosity, embracing challenges, and turning ideas into meaningful action, we unlock possibilities far more valuable than any precious metal. The greatest wealth is not buried beneath the ground—it is created within the human mind and shared through innovation, character, and the courage to bring new ideas into the world.

items.headline: How to pack 200 years worth of ideas into a book? Arunava Sinha on the limitations and structure of 'The Bengal Reader'
items.body: 'The Bengal Reader' book cover; and editor and translator Arunava Sinha. (Images via Aleph Book Company and Arunava Sinha) ‘The Bengal Reader’ is a massive book of Bengali fiction and nonfiction, by any measure. At 596 pages, it contains excerpts from essays, plays, novels and poems by stalwarts like social reformer Rammohun Roy, Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore, filmmakers Satyajit Ray and Ritwik Ghatak, scientist Jagadish Chandra Bose, and novelist/poet Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. It covers some 200 years’ worth of ideas and writing, arranged chronologically. Its size notwithstanding, it is a tasting menu of sorts - an introduction to some of the most important thinkers and writers from Bengal from the 19th century on, rather than a deep engagement with any one of them. In an online video interview with Moneycontrol, editor-cum-translator of the work Arunava Sinha spoke about how he became involved with 'The Bengal Reader' , how he selected the works and why he could not include works by the Kamal Kumar Majumdar among others in his Bengal compendium. Excerpts: How did this project come about? ‘The Bengal Reader’ contains works from over 130 writers. So, obviously it includes a wide variety of forms. Fiction in the form of short stories and in the form of excerpts from novels, poems, essays, early works of polemic — the first writers in Bangla, for example, were people like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, who were using their writing to drive their ideas for social reform; so I would refer to them as polemics. There’s some political writing, there’s letters, there’s even graffiti, there’s a pamphlet. There are some excerpts from plays. In fact, it has more fiction in the form of short stories than ‘The Greatest Bengali Stories Ever Told’. The idea actually came from David Davidar, who is the publisher of Aleph Book Company, who published ‘The Greatest Bengali Stories Ever Told’. He came to me and said, why don’t you do a compendium of Bengali writing over the years? So we went a little back and forth about whether it should be a group — fiction, essays, poetry and so on. Eventually I said it might be more interesting to present the pieces in chronological order, rather than by form. Related Stories Why ‘Drown All the Refugees’—about migration and loss—is the Indian gothic novel to read in ... ‘Days at the Morisaki Bookshop’ author: Wouldn’t write if I were the only person left on Earth Accel India Partner Subrata Mitra: When entrepreneurs do interesting stuff, the investors follow So that's what we have finally done, and there’s approximately 200 years’ worth of writing in there, starting with Raja Ram Mohun Roy’s arguments against Sati , and ending with a writer who writes under a pseudonym, and it is a sort of memoir of a gay young man who is writing from a foreign country, and of course it’s written in Bengali. And in-between, there is a whole bunch of other pieces, which will really go across all forms, all areas, all styles. Did you pick the chronological order to give readers a sense of the period the writers were writing in? How did you make the selection? Any piece that belongs to a particular period will in some way be talking to that period as well, and it is easier to figure that out, to try and relate it to what was happening around that time, but that’s something that I’m trying to be explicit about. I’m not saying read these things through these pieces, but there is a certain amount of history that’s inevitably found. I was more interested in the chronological aspect (to show) how the writing has grown and evolved and changed. While selecting the works for translation, were you thinking about giving readers a larger sense of Bengali writing, of prevalent ideas, of popular movements, and in terms of introducing us to the biggest thinkers and writers in the language? Were you worried about any of the pieces in terms of how they would be received now versus when they were written? Primarily, I envisage ‘The Bengal Reader’ as a reading project. It is not so much a literary project as it is meant to let the reader embark on a reading project that enables them to read across 200 years in a way that normally you would not be able to do if you picked up individual books. An 1830s portrait of Raja Rammohun Roy by Henry Perronet Briggs, at the Bristol Museums, Galleries & Archives. 'The Bengal Reader' begins with an essay by Roy. (Image via Wikimedia Commons) You would have had to leave some things out of the project as well. Oh, plenty. These were hard decisions. Some pieces I had translated and were ready, but we had to leave them out because we couldn’t possibly take the book to any more than 600 pages. And some were hard to come by, by way of securing rights. And some writers were extremely literary; I would not be able to assist them with short articles. Could you an give an example of something/someone you had to leave out, where copyright and author permissions weren’t an issue? There’s a writer called Kamal Kumar Majumdar, who wrote a kind of prose that was unique. She wrote in modern times, but wrote in a prose that you couldn’t actually bring down to a particular period. And she’s a writer whom you have to read at length to try and get something out of. I actually translated an entire story of his. Then I left it out because I felt that I would have to do a lot more work on that story to get it anywhere close to what he was trying to achieve. And the time that I had to finish this would not allow me to do it. Translations seem to be taking off. Is that also your sense of this world — both in terms of volume and quality of translations? It’s also of uneven quality. A lot more publishers, not just the established publishers, but a lot of smaller publishers have also started publishing translations. And, quite honestly, some of those translations they publish are very good. But certainly I think people are talking much more about translations. They’re much more aware about the fact that you can read the vast and wide literatures of India in a language of your choice. But I am not sure that the numbers suggest that they’re actually reading it. Books like ‘Heart Lamp’ or ‘Tomb of Sand’ sell in huge numbers because they won the International Book Award. And then other books in translation, (the difference in sales figures) is so huge that you realize that it’s a prize-led trend rather than lifting all boats — far from it. And in some ways, because more translations are being published and because serious fiction anyway has seen fewer readers, there’s a dwindling number of readers for serious fiction. These two things have contributed, actually, to fewer copies of each translated book being sold and read, even if translated literature as a whole may have more readers because there are more books. 'The Bengal Reader' also has writing by filmmakers like Satyajit Ray (above) and Ritwik Ghatak. (Image via Wikimedia Commons) Is there movement towards translating bestsellers in popular Indian fiction, and not just serious writing? It would be worth checking whether whatever made them a bestseller in their own language would also mean — if not a bestseller, but — at least a fair amount of readership in another language, which could be English or another non-English Indian language. So, certainly, I would love to see more of that. Speaking to translators, it seems that the industry — even as it is growing — is missing some of the desired structure and guardrails. In that, the process right now is that the translator picks a piece of writing they are interested to work on, then they chase the writer or the writer’s family or estate for rights , then they do the translation work, and then mostly the publisher will come in towards the end to purchase the work and publish it. Is that a good way of doing things? Yes, that’s pretty much it. And I wouldn’t say it’s a good way of doing it at all. There are many ways through which publishers arrive at the decision of which books to publish. For example, they have those who are experts in that language recommending books, someone will read it and then give their opinion on whether this book is worth pursuing. Then they will ask a translator, for example. All of these are great because they’re taking the time of the expert in question, and only after that is the decision taken and the company makes it. Now, this in some ways also acts as a form of gatekeeping, but the fact is that it ensures that whatever is published is of high quality, even if many other good books also get left out. It is a bit sad that the only similar process through which Indian translators can go through, is actually run by ACT (Ashoka Centre for Translation) along with SALT, which is a UK and US-based organisation of Asian literature in translations. They send out calls twice a year for translators to submit proposals and then select some of those translators to produce samples. And then they further identify the winners among those and then put them up on their website and spread the word so that publishers who might be interested — in terms of selection, they have done the hard work and they have a jury of experts and so on. Something like this should be happening in India all the time. Our English-language publishing industry is, at the end of the day, no more than 25–30 years old. This is something that we need to — and I think we will — get our own version of. In terms of translations from non-English to non-English Indian languages, are there any interesting examples that you have seen that are working well? There are quite a few translations now going into Hindi, where publishers — because they have a much wider base of readers — can also afford to perhaps take a few risks. There are translations of works from Kannada, from Bangla, from Gujarati, from Marathi, from Tamil that are going into Hindi. There are big Hindi publishers (like) Vani Prakashan and Rajkamal, who have been publishing such books. It is very exciting. Malayalam also is a great recipient of translations from other languages. Marathi also does quite a bit. I just hope that the other languages will also follow suit. In this context, I must also mention the initiative taken by the Tamil Nadu government to get Tamil literature out in translation in other languages and supported by grants. It is something that actually began a long time ago with the literatures from the South. Mini Krishnan used to write a series and she got funding from (MR AR Educational Society of Madras for 50 translations).
items.snippet: What did Rammohun Roy say about Sati? What was Mahasweta Devi's critique of consumerism? What did Meghnad Saha really say about cues to modern science in the Vedas? How did Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay tell the story of Devdas, before it inspired movie after movie? In 'The Bengal Reader', Arunava Sinha offers translated excerpts from some of the biggest thinkers and writers in Bengali over the last 200 years. An interview with Arunava Sinha about 'The Bengal Reader' and the practice of translation in India.

items.headline: May require only minor corrections in mobile tariff hikes, says Vodafone-Idea
items.body: Telecom services provider, Vodafone-Idea (Vi) on Friday said that it has no plan to go for an across-the-board hike in mobile tariff and may opt for only minor corrections in the existing rates. “Minor corrections will be there but not a structural hike as you generally see... Ongoing minor tariff corrections driven by current market conditions,” Abhijit Kishore, Chief Executive Officer, Vi said here on the sidelines of the Cellular Operators Association of India DigiCom Summit 2026. Historical Trends Recently, Bharti Airtel has increased prepaid mobile recharge plans by around 4-5 per cent and analysts have projected that telecom operators may raise tariff by about 15 per cent by June this year, two years after the last major adjustments, a timeline that aligns with historical industry trends. Analysts have said that recharge price hike and strategic pricing adjustments are expected to accelerate sector revenue growth to 16 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in FY27, a significant jump from the estimated 7 per cent YoY growth for FY26. Meanwhile, Kishore said that the government has shown confidence in the company as a significant shareholder and the company is focussing on improving performance. Subscriber Addition “The government is a 49 per cent stakeholder and we really value that. We are working towards what we should be doing, which is basically improving the performance, which is what you see on the subscriber initiative. We have reported earlier in the month of February-March, which is out in the public domain,” he added. After recording a decline in subscriber base in the last few years, Vi has shown improvement in subscriber addition for two consecutive months – in February and March this year. The company has added over one-lakh mobile subscribers in March, according to the latest monthly report by Telecom Regulatory Authority of India. Reliance Jio has not announced any price hike in its tariff plans yet. Published on April 24, 2026
items.snippet: Vodafone-Idea plans minor mobile tariff adjustments, emphasizing subscriber growth and confidence from the government's significant stake.

items.headline: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: REC, SBI, Vodafone Idea, Kalyan Jewellers and more
items.body: The markets are firm in afternoon trade. The Nifty 50 is cruising comfortably above 25,800 while the BSE Sensex garnered close to a 500-point gain in afternoon trade.  The Index gains look steady on the surface, but the big action sat firmly in individual counters, where earnings, balance-sheet strength, promoter moves and policy-linked developments drove sharp, sometimes uncomfortable price swings. Here are the top movers and shakers at this hour: State Bank of India State Bank of India share price jumped 6.7% by midday, extending gains after the lender delivered a better-than-expected December quarter. The stock touched a fresh lifetime high during the session, backed by heavy volumes and broad-based buying across PSU banks. The rally in SBI spilled over into the wider public-sector banking space, with the PSU Bank index rising more than 3.4%, and all constituents trading in the green. The market response was direct and unsentimental. Strong numbers were rewarded, scale was valued, and SBI sat right at the centre of that trade. ALSO READSilver, Gold ETFs surge as COMEX silver jumps over 6%, MCX price soars 5% Shipping Corporation of India Shipping Corporation of India surged nearly 15.8%, marking its strongest single-session move in almost four years. The sharp rally followed a decisive improvement in the December-quarter performance, where net profit rose more than five times to Rs 405 crore. Revenue grew 23% to Rs 1,612 crore, while tighter cost control stood out, with total expenses down 2% and finance costs lower by 24%. The stock reaction was aggressive, fuelled by the sudden clarity that earnings momentum had returned faster than expected. Vodafone Idea Vodafone Idea gained about 4% by midday, with volumes swelling through the session. The stock moved after promoter Kumar Mangalam Birla bought an additional 4.09 crore equity shares via the open market. That single action carried weight. It did not change the company’s structural challenges, but it did send a message on commitment, and the market responded in its own blunt way, pushing the stock higher even as the broader telecom space stayed mixed. ALSO READJewellery stocks soar after India-US trade deal: Kalyan Jewellers jumps 11%, Titan surges Kalyan Jewellers Kalyan Jewellers India rallied over 12%, reacting sharply to a strong December-quarter performance. Consolidated net profit jumped 90.4% to Rs 416.29 crore, while revenue from operations rose 42.1% to Rs 10,343.41 crore. International operations also delivered, with revenue up 38% to Rs 1,164 crore. The numbers left little room for ambiguity, and the stock price adjusted quickly, without hesitation. Suzlon Energy Suzlon Energy was marginally lower, down about 0.04%, after an early uptick faded. The company reported a nearly 15% rise in December-quarter net profit to Rs 445 crore, supported by revenue growth to Rs 4,228 crore and a record order book of 6.4 GW. Despite that, profit booking set in after recent gains, and the stock slipped back toward flat territory. The reaction was restrained, not dismissive, but clearly cautious. REC  REC shares declined 2.4% by midday, even as the stock remained in focus following developments around the proposed PFC–REC merger flagged in the Union Budget. The plan, which would see REC merged into PFC with a swap ratio of 8 PFC shares for every 9 REC shares, aims to create a lending entity with a combined loan book of about Rs 11.5 trillion. The market response, however, leaned defensive in the short term, reflecting uncertainty around valuation, structure and execution rather than outright rejection of the proposal.
items.snippet: Indian markets stayed firm at midday as stock-specific action dominated. SBI hit record highs, Kalyan Jewellers surged on strong Q3 numbers, while REC slipped amid merger uncertainty and Vodafone Idea gained after promoter buying.

items.headline: Birla ups stake in Vodafone Idea via market purchases
items.body: Aditya Birla Group chairman Kumar Mangalam Birla has increased his personal stake in Vodafone Idea through open market purchases in four tranches between January end and first week of February . Birla purchased 22.1 million shares on January 30, 18.8 million shares on February 1, t4.5 million shares on February 2, and 14.2 million shares on February 3 taking his cumulative acquisition to 59.6 million shares for a total outlay of Rs 66.18 crore across tranches. What does shareholding data reflect? Shareholding data as of December 31, 2025 showed Birla individually holding a 0.02% stake in Vodafone Idea, while the promoter and promoter group together owned 25.57% of the company. Public shareholders held the remaining 74.43%, including 49% by the government of India through conversion of debt to equity in various lots over the past three years. Birla’s holding after the latest buys now amounts to 0.07%. ALSO READL&T wins Rs 1,000–2,500 crore Dubai road project; shares jump 1% The marginal but symbolic increase in Birla’s direct ownership and signals promoter confidence in the company, analysts said. The distressed telco during its fiscal third quarter earnings call unveiled its recovery roadmap detailing efforts to strengthen its capital structure and expand network investments. The stake purchase also reinforces the commitment articulated by the promoter group during the same earnings call, when management reiterated its willingness to support Vodafone Idea’s turnaround journey. “We have invested Rs 27,000 crore in last few years. ALSO READKPI Green Energy wins Adani Group orders for 300 MW Khavda renewable project, total capacity rises to 834 MWac That itself gives a message that (the) promoters always have remained confident, they've invested and would make sure that if there is a need, they support (the) company,” Sushil Agarwal, Group CFO, Aditya Birla Group had said. Vodafone Idea's three-year revival strategy During the earnings presentation, Vodafone Idea had outlined a three-year revival strategy backed by a planned Rs 45,000 crore investment programme aimed at restoring network competitiveness and improving customer experience. The company has been prioritising investments in radio access network expansion, coverage parity in priority circles, capacity augmentation and deeper indoor coverage. Management has also indicated plans to scale its 5G footprint across additional cities and explore opportunities in fixed wireless access to compete more effectively with peers. In a recent report, analysts at Emkay Global said recent regulatory relief on adjusted gross revenue liabilities has materially improved Vodafone Idea’s financial viability. “The Union Cabinet’s decision to freeze AGR dues of ~Rs 87,700 crore, allow long-term staggered repayment till FY41, and initiate reassessment (including potential interest/penalty reversal) materially reduces near-term cash outflows and insolvency risk. This meaningfully improves VI’s ability to operate as a going concern and invest in the network,” Emkay analysts noted. They added that with the freezing of dues, the net present value of the AGR dues drops to Rs500bn, versus Rs870bn earlier, with a further scope for reduction in liabilities in case of a favourable outcome of recalculation and reconciliation. However, the brokerage cautioned that the company’s long-term recovery will hinge on its ability to execute network expansion effectively. Vodafone Idea shares dipped 0.86% on Tuesday on the Bombay Stock Exchange at Rs 11.48 per share at end of trading hours.
items.snippet: Kumar Mangalam Birla has increased his personal stake in Vodafone Idea through open market purchases worth Rs 66.18 crore, a symbolic move signalling promoter confidence amid the telco’s revival push.

items.headline: COAI seeks reduction in TRAI-recommended spectrum auction price, moots idea of free radiowaves
items.body: Ahead of the next spectrum auction, the telecom industry body COAI has urged the government to lower bid prices, saying service providers have yet to recover their huge investments in 5G infrastructure, according to an official. Speaking with PTI on the sidelines of the recently held COAI Digicom Summit, Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) Director General S P Kochhar said that the industry expects the government to consider the humongous investment made by telecom operators in 5G, without any return on investment. "I hope that the spectrum prices go down because 5G has seen a lot of capital infusion without ROI. Till the time we start getting ROI, investing in a very expensive spectrum will have to be judged as a cost-effective business purpose. A spectrum cannot be just used by picking it up from the auction, but it has to be made usable with large investments," Kocchar said. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) in February recommended that the government put the entire 11,790 MHz of available spectrum in the frequency bands of 600 MHz, 800 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, 2100 MHz, 2300 MHz, 2500 MHz, 3300 MHz and 26 GHz for auction. Spectrum with low frequency count provide wider coverage. The government is exploring auctioning spectrum in the 600 MHz band, which is expected to improve mobile network coverage inside buildings. The regulator's recommended base price values the entire spectrum at ₹2.1 lakh crore. The recommended price is estimated to be 19 per cent cheaper than prices recommended for the last auction held in 2022. Kocchar said that the costing will decide as quantum of spectrum that telecom operators will buy. "We want more spectrum. There are many countries where the spectrum is free, but there are obligations for that spectrum. So the model has to evolve now, with 5G having come in and 6G on the horizon. The model has to be different from the one which we are following. That is a call the government has to take," Kocchar said. The government has decided to allocate spectrum administratively without auction for satellite communication services. However, spectrum available for mobile services is allocated only through auction. "We have been writing to the government that the spectrum cost is the biggest capital expenditure that we incur. They have to at least hold a hand till the time we start getting ROI on the use of spectrum," Kochhar said. Published on April 26, 2026

items.headline: 'I was in denial with the idea of quick commerceâ: BigBasket founder Hari Menon
items.body: BigBasket founder Hari Menon, in a LinkedIn post, said he was initially in denial about the idea of quick commerce.Penning his thoughts as he steps down as chief executive nearly 15 years after launching the online grocery startup, Menon reflected on how consumer behaviour changed faster than many expected.âIf you had asked 100 people back then whether they wanted groceries in 10 minsâ¦ most wouldâve said no. But the moment we gave it to our customers, they lapped it up,â he wrote.Today, the company operates more than 900 dark stores across more than 60 cities, said Menon, who added that BigBasket is âunrecognisableâ compared to its early years.Remembering the company's early days, Menon said the team had no template for what their goal was: helping Indian households access fresh and reliable groceries.âBut we knew the four things we had to get right and that nothing else mattered until we did: order fill rate, on-time delivery, having 95% of our SKUs stocked at any given time, and the best of customer satisfaction,â he said.Founded in 2011, BigBasket built its business around scheduled grocery deliveries and was initially reluctant to embrace quick commerce because of concerns over its cash-intensive economics.However, the rapid rise of Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and Zepto accelerated consumer adoption of 10-minute delivery services, particularly in urban India.Once the country's largest online grocer, BigBasket steadily lost market share to quick commerce rivals. In August 2024, the company fully pivoted to quick commerce.Passing the batonMenon is handing over the âbatonâ to former Amazon executive Amit Nanda, who will take over as chief executive. âHe brings such sharp instincts, deep consumer understanding, and exactly the kind of energy this next phase needs,â Menon said in the post.Menon will continue to serve on the company's board.ET had first reported in September 2025 that Menon's tenure was nearing its end following the Tata Group's acquisition of the Bengaluru-based company in 2021, as succession planning gathered pace.BigBasket's leadership transition comes at a challenging time for the company, which reported a decline in turnover in FY25 as competition intensified.However, in an April interview, Tata Digital chief executive and BigBasket chairman Sajith Sivanandan said the firm was starting to see early signs of recovery of lost market share, with the platform accounting for one in every five new app downloads.He added that BigBasket's differentiation would come from quality and private labels such as Fresho and BB Royal â brands Menon says he is âenormously proud ofââ â rather than competing solely on speed or pricing
items.snippet: BigBasket founder Hari Menon is stepping down as CEO after 15 years, reflecting on the company's evolution from scheduled deliveries to embracing quick commerce. Initially skeptical, Menon witnessed rapid consumer adoption of 10-minute grocery services, a shift that reshaped the market.  He passes the leadership baton to Amit Nanda, aiming to navigate intensified competition and regain market share through quality and private labels.

Only in Bengaluru, you can sit next to a sitting MP of Bengaluru and pitch your startup on Namma metro pic.twitter.com/mkC3TG1p3M — Anil Pai (@anilbpai) June 26, 2026 The post quickly attracted attention online, with many users highlighting Bengaluru's unique blend of technology, entrepreneurship, and public life. items.headline: Airtel leads subscriber gains in May as Vodafone Idea extends recovery; Jio remains No. 1
items.body: . Vodafone Idea added wireless subscribers for the third consecutive month in May, extending a gradual recovery in customer numbers even as Bharti Airtel emerged as the biggest net gainer and Reliance Jio retained its market leadership, according to data from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India. Vi added 121,289 wireless subscribers during May, taking its total base to 198.66 million from 198.54 million in April, continuing a positive run after years of prolonged customer losses. Bharti Airtel was the largest net gainer, adding 2.93 million wireless subscribers, while Reliance Jio added 2.15 million. State-run BSNL lost 104,660 subscribers. Overall, India's wireless subscriber base expanded by 5.09 million to 1.277 billion at end-May. Jio continued to dominate the market with 501.44 million wireless subscribers, followed by Airtel with 483.81 million, Vi with 198.66 million and BSNL with 92.91 million. The total wireless subscriber base, including fixed wireless access connections, rose by 5.50 million to 1.294 billion during May, while total telephone subscribers reached 1.343 billion. Tele-density improved to 94.02 percent from 93.69 percent in April. Related Stories BSNL proposes Rs 77,000 crore capex over five years, targets 2 lakh more 4G sites Telcos rethink 5G FWA push as rising costs, churn strengthen case for fibre Airtel’s Nxtra to quadruple data centre capacity to 1GW as AI demand drives growth: CLSA Active wireless subscribers stood at 1.196 billion, representing 93.64 percent of the total base. Airtel had the highest proportion of active subscribers among the major operators, with a VLR ratio of 99.28 percent, against 98.83 percent for Jio, 84.41 percent for Vi and 55.85 percent for BSNL. Demand for operator switching remained elevated, with 14.46 million users submitting mobile number portability requests during May.
