My parents didn’t support the decision at the time, I felt embarrassed at family gatherings, and my first freelancing gig was just ₹10,000/month,” she wrote.She also spoke about doubting herself during that phase and questioning whether she had made the wrong decision. “There were many nights where I thought I had made a mistake.”Still, she continued working on content creation and freelancing projects. According to her, consistency slowly helped her build a different career path. “But I kept going. I showed up, created content almost every day, and figured things out along the way.” How freelancing helpedAs time passed, she started getting more clients and eventually moved into storytelling, social media strategy, and UGC work. Around 14 months after leaving her legal job, she said her earnings had increased to nearly Rs 2 lakh per month.“Slowly, things started working. Clients came in, I found my strength in storytelling, moved into social media strategy + UGC, and within 14 months, I was earning ₹2L/month.”But she also made it clear that the change was not only about income. For her, the biggest shift was getting back control over her time and daily routine.131282252'Success' does not have to mean working all dayIn her post, she questioned the common belief that success only comes through extremely long working hours. “But this isn’t just about money. It’s about this idea we’ve all been taught, that you need to work 12–14 hours a day to succeed. I don’t agree.”She said her current lifestyle allows her to work fewer hours while still having time for herself, family, and hobbies. “I work ~6 hours a day now. I go to cafés, play pickleball, go to the gym, spend time with family, and actually enjoy my life.”Ending her post, she encouraged people to stop measuring success only through traditional expectations or outside pressure. “You don’t have to follow my path. You don’t have to quit your job. But don’t let anyone define what ‘hard work’ or ‘success’ should look like for you. If your life doesn’t feel right, you’re allowed to choose differently.”
items.snippet: A young lawyer who was earning around Rs 1 lakh a month left her corporate job after feeling constantly stressed, exhausted, and unhappy with her daily life. In an Instagram post, Mehar Verma shared how long working hours and burnout pushed her to quit without a backup plan. Despite struggling in the beginning and earning just Rs 10,000 from her first freelancing project, she continued creating content and eventually built a career in storytelling, social media strategy, and UGC.

items.headline: DoT extends Vodafone Idea AGR reassessment deadline to June 30 amid data hurdles
items.body: Vodafone Idea IC8 Watchlist Portfolio Message Follow NSE/BSE Select NSE LIVE BSE LIVE Day High Day Low Volume (NSE) More × Add to Watchlist The department of telecommunications (DoT) has pushed the deadline for reassessing adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues of Vodafone Idea by three months to June 30, as field officials continue to face difficulties in completing the exercise, sources told Moneycontrol. The extension comes after the Supreme Court allowed the Centre to recalculate the telco’s AGR liabilities for the FY07-FY19 period. Following thg order, the cabinet in January cleared the reassessment process, directing DoT’s Controller of Communication Accounts (CCAs) — its field units — to review licence fee and spectrum usage charge payments made by the company based on AGR within the stipulated timeline. The initial deadline for completion was February 22, with a committee assigned to finalise the exercise by March 31. While the reassessment of licence fees has already been completed, the recalculation of spectrum usage charges is still in progress, sources said. They added that the CCAs have encountered operational issues, largely due to gaps in documentation. In several telecom circles, Vodafone Idea has been unable to provide legacy records required for validation, slowing progress. Related Stories Vodafone Idea steps up capex as Rs 6,400 crore funding raised, lender talks advance Stocks to Watch Today: IRB Infra, Lupin, Bharat Electronics, Zen Tech, Lumax Auto, BSE, Wipro, PC Je... BSNL, Vodafone Idea discuss deeper 4G, 5G tower sharing; data centres, AI, cloud among potential are... “Given these bottlenecks, the deadline has been extended to allow more time for data reconciliation and completion of the exercise,” a source said. The government holds around 49 percent stake in Vodafone Idea after converting about Rs 53,083 crore of dues into equity in February 2023 and April 2025. Queries sent to Vodafone Idea and DoT didn’t elicit any response. The reassessment stems from Supreme Court rulings in October and November that allowed a fresh calculation of AGR dues. The cabinet on December 31 approved relief measures, including freezing the company’s Rs 87,695 crore AGR liability as of December-end. Vodafone Idea has been allowed to repay these dues over FY32 to FY41. DoT, in a January communications to CCAs, said AGR dues for FY07-FY19 —excluding amounts already upheld by the Supreme Court’s September 1, 2020 ruling — would be reassessed using February 3, 2020 deduction verification guidelines and relevant audit reports. According to sources, the exercise could potentially reduce the company’s final AGR burden significantly. Under the revised payment plan, Vodafone Idea will pay Rs 744 crore between March 2026 and March 2031, with annual outgo capped at Rs 124 crore. This will be followed by yearly payments of Rs 100 crore from March 2032 to March 2035, with the remaining dues to be cleared in equal instalments between March 2036 and March 2041, the company said in a January 9 exchange filing.
items.snippet: This extension comes after a Supreme Court order allowed the Centre to recalculate the telco’s AGR liabilities for the the FY07-FY19 period

items.headline: Quote of the day by Socrates: "Strong minds discuss ideas, average minds discuss..."
items.body: Socrates Socrates urged meaningful dialogue over gossip and trivial events He stresses intellectual growth via idea-focused discussions The Socratic method promotes critical thinking and deeper inquiry Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan In an age where conversations often drift towards gossip and fleeting events, the enduring wisdom of Socrates reminds us of the true value of thoughtful dialogue. His well-known quote, “ Strong minds discuss ideas, average minds discuss events, and weak minds discuss people, ” continues to hold relevance, encouraging individuals to rise above superficial discussions and engage in meaningful thinking. This insight reflects the essence of intellectual growth and disciplined thought. Who was Socrates? Socrates, one of the earliest and most influential thinkers of ancient Greece, laid the foundation of Western philosophy. Born in Athens, he dedicated his life to exploring questions about ethics, morals, and human behaviour. Unlike many philosophers, Socrates did not leave behind written works. His teachings are known through the accounts of his students, particularly Plato and Xenophon, who preserved his ideas in the form of dialogues. Meaning of the quote In this quote, Socrates conveys that the nature of a person's conversations reflects the strength of their mind. He suggests that those who engage with ideas are driven by curiosity, learning, and a desire to understand deeper truths, which ultimately leads to intellectual growth. In contrast, discussions limited to events remain surface-level, while conversations focused on people often drift into gossip and distraction. The message highlights that true wisdom lies in rising above trivial matters and developing the habit of thoughtful, idea-driven dialogue, as it shapes clearer thinking, better judgment, and a more meaningful approach to life. The Socratic method and its relevance Socrates is also known for introducing a unique method of inquiry based on questioning. Instead of offering direct answers, he would ask a series of probing questions to challenge assumptions and reveal more profound understanding. This approach, now known as the Socratic method, remains widely used in education and philosophy to promote critical thinking. In contemporary times, where distractions are abundant, the message of this quote is particularly significant. Meaningful conversations that revolve around ideas not only sharpen the mind but also contribute to personal and social growth. Avoiding unnecessary criticism or gossip helps maintain clarity, focus, and respect in communication. Socrates’ words serve as a reminder that the quality of our thoughts and conversations defines the strength of our minds. By choosing to engage with ideas rather than distractions, individuals can cultivate wisdom, discipline, and a deeper understanding of life.
items.snippet: Socrates’ timeless quote urges focusing on ideas over gossip, highlighting the importance of meaningful conversations, critical thinking, and intellectual growth in everyday life.

items.headline: 'People have no idea': Engineer highlights how Google protects families after employee death
items.body: The post highlighted Google’s death benefits. (Image credit: Reuters) Oracle laid off up to 30,000 employees in a single email. Google's death benefits for employees go viral on X. Google gives spouse pay, stock, and child support after death Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Oracle shocked the tech world by laying off between 20,000 and 30,000 employees through a single 6 am email, leaving thousands facing sudden uncertainty. The massive cut comes amid a wave of tech industry restructuring, raising questions about employee security in a volatile market. Amid the layoffs, a post on X has gone viral, drawing attention to how Google handles employee security. The post highlighted Google’s death benefits, which include a spouse receiving 50% of the salary for 10 years, all unvested stock vesting immediately, children receiving $1,000 per month until age 19 (or 23 if full-time students), and the benefits apply even to brand new hires. A X user @aakashgupta broke down the numbers for a senior engineer: a spouse could receive $925,000 over a decade, a $555,000 life insurance payout, $350,000 in stock, and $1,000 per child per month -- totalling over $1.85 million before vested stock. There’s no tenure required, so even a new hire gets the same benefits as a longtime employee. He added that the policy, designed by ex-Google HP chief Laszlo Bock in 2012, reflects the belief that family security is a duty nets cost the $350 billion company very little. Run the math on what this actually pays out. Related Stories 5,000 questions an hour are hitting ChatTJB. The twist? One man answers them all 'FAANG level company': Software engineer shares how salary grew from Rs 37,000 to Rs 2.2 crore Techie laid off 8 months ago on struggle to find new job: ‘Offers were lower than…’ Median Google employee made $331,894 in 2024. The death benefit is 50% of base salary, capped at $12,500/month. On top of that, the spouse gets a lump sum life insurance payout of 3x annual base salary, up to $2.5 million. All… https://t.co/mbKiAn6IKA — Aakash Gupta (@aakashgupta) April 4, 2026 The post went viral, drawing widespread reactions from users about employee safety and corporate responsibility. One user wrote, “And here my manager thinks giving a work-from-home on Saturday is a huge favour. Google is really out there taking care of employees even after they are gone. Definition of Life Goals.” Another person said, “The death benefit package at Google really is extraordinary — most people have no idea how valuable it is until they actually do the math. The $2.5M life insurance cap plus 10 years of salary continuation for spouses would be unthinkable at most companies. Makes you think twice about the total comp picture beyond base.” A third user added, “Rare to see companies think long term like this.”
items.snippet: Amid a wave of layoffs across tech companies, an X user explains how Google provides generous death benefits to employees’ families, even for new hires

items.headline: Vodafone Idea shares jump 2% to a fresh record high, rally over 100% in 1 year. What’s ahead?
items.body: The shares of Vodafone Idea jumped more than 2% to hit a fresh record high on Monday, extending its gaining streak for the fifth consecutive session, with the technical structure indicating further bullish movement ahead.The shares of the telecom major rose to a new 52-week high of Rs 14.06 apiece in the morning trading hours of Monday. Notably, this is the first time the stock has crossed the Rs 14-mark since September 2024. The stock has gained around 9% in one week, and a whopping 47% in just a month. Vodafone Idea shares have delivered around 107% returns in one year, 100% in three years and more than 63% in five years. The stock is up over 20% so far in 2026.Last week, Vodafone Idea reported a net profit of Rs 51,970 crore for the January-March quarter of the financial year 2026, as against a net loss of Rs 7,166 crore in the year-ago period, primarily driven by a one-time accounting gain related to the reassessment of AGR dues and recognition of the present value of future AGR payments.The firm’s revenue from operations meanwhile rose 3% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 11,332 crore during the quarter which ended on March 31, 2026, from Rs 11,017 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. EBITDA grew 4.9% YoY to Rs 4,889 crore, while Average revenue per user, or ARPU, rose to Rs 190 from Rs 175 in the year-ago quarter, marking an 8.3% increase.In the beginning of May, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) reduced the telco’s adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues by 27% to Rs 64,046 crore as of December 31, resulting in bullish calls for the stock. Later, the stock jumped after the company named billionaire industrialist Kumar Mangalam Birla as its non-executive chairman, around five years after he resigned from the same role in the telecom giant amid financial stress.Should you buy, sell or hold Vodafone Idea shares?Vodafone Idea shares continue to trade well above its key short- and long-term moving averages, reflecting a strong bullish trend, said Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities. “The RSI stands at 84.75, while the ADX is at 65, indicating extremely elevated momentum levels where intermittent profit booking cannot be ruled out,” he said.Since hitting a low of 8.13 on April 2, the stock has rallied nearly 71%, highlighting strong buying interest, Sha highlighted. “On the weekly chart, the stock has broken above its previous swing high of 10.25 and is sustaining above it, which further strengthens the bullish structure. Rising MACD histogram bars also reinforce the positive momentum. The 12–12.5 zone is expected to act as a crucial support, and the trend is likely to remain bullish as long as the stock sustains above this range,” he said.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea shares surged to a new record high on Monday, extending a winning streak. The telecom major's stock has seen significant gains over the past week, month, and year. Recent financial results showed a net profit for the January-March quarter, a turnaround from the previous year. Revenue and ARPU also saw increases.

items.headline: Concert outfit ideas: What to wear without overplanning a rockstar-like look
items.body: From breezy fits to bold accessories, here’s how to dress for music festivals without compromising on style. (Pic: Pinterest) Choose breathable fabrics and loose fits for concert comfort Layer lightly with shirts or jackets for style and practicality Accessorize boldly but keep bags small and makeup fresh Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan There’s something about music concerts and rock festivals that makes getting dressed part of the experience. It’s not just about looking good for pictures. It’s about wearing something that lets you move, stay comfortable, and still feel like you made an effort. With the heat, crowds, and long hours, the trick is simple. Keep it light, keep it practical, but don’t play it safe. Concert dressing is one of the few times you can push your style a little without it feeling out of place. Start with pieces that breathe Before you think about trends, think about the weather. Breathable fabrics and easy silhouettes will take you much further than anything overly styled. Shorts, mini skirts, and airy dresses are obvious choices, but they work for a reason. They’re easy, comfortable, and give you room to move. If you’re more of a pants person, go for loose fits like cargo pants or wide-leg trousers in lighter fabrics. They hold structure without trapping heat. Also Read: Faux leather, reworked: The unexpected summer trend making its way into SS’26 wardrobes Layer, but keep it smart Layering at a summer concert is less about warmth and more about styling. Think lightweight shirts worn open, cropped jackets, or even a scarf tied loosely for texture. A denim jacket or an oversized shirt works well for late evenings when the temperature drops slightly. The key is to carry something that adds to your look without weighing you down. Pick a vibe and build around it Concert dressing becomes easier when you decide on a mood. A rock-chic look can be as simple as a fitted tank, leather or faux leather shorts, and boots. Add a belt, a slightly messy hairstyle , and you’re done. If you lean towards boho, flowy dresses, crochet tops, or tiered skirts work well. Earthy tones, layered jewellery, and easy sandals complete the look without trying too hard. The “summer girl” vibe is lighter and more playful. Think crop tops, denim shorts, bright colours, and minimal layers. It’s relaxed but still put-together. For something more urban, streetwear works well in a concert setting. Oversized tees, cargos, sneakers, and statement sunglasses create a look that feels current without being uncomfortable. Accessories that do the work Accessories are where you can have the most fun. A statement belt, layered chains, chunky rings, or bold earrings can completely change a simple outfit. Boots instantly add edge, while sneakers keep things practical. If you’re planning to be on your feet all night, comfort matters more than anything else. Bags should stay small and easy. Crossbody styles or mini slings work best so you don’t have to think about them once you’re inside. Also Read: Style tips: Spring summer trends are a win-win for curvy girls, here’s how to get it right Makeup, but lighter Summer concerts and heavy makeup don’t always get along. Go for skin that looks fresh, a bit of gloss, and maybe a bold liner or shimmer if you want to stand out. This is also where you can experiment. Glitter, subtle sparkle, or even temporary tattoos can add just enough detail without feeling overdone. The best part is that it’s not about getting every detail right but feeling comfortable enough to enjoy the music, the crowd, and the moment.
items.snippet: The best concert outfits are the ones you don’t have to adjust every ten minutes. You can dance, walk, sit, and move around without thinking twice

items.headline: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: 'Every breakthrough business idea begins with solving a common problem.
items.body: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: Successful businesses are often built around one simple idea: solving a problem that affects many people. Throughout history, entrepreneurs have identified inefficiencies, high costs, or gaps in the market and turned those challenges into opportunities for innovation. In technology especially, some of the biggest companies emerged because their founders questioned why products were expensive, inaccessible, or unnecessarily complicated. As industries continue evolving rapidly, business leaders frequently emphasize that entrepreneurship is not only about creating something new, but about recognizing problems others overlook and finding better ways to solve them.Quote of the Day Today: Michael Dell on Entrepreneurship and InnovationThat mindset is reflected in a quote by Michael Dell, founder of Dell Technologies, he said, “Every breakthrough business idea begins with solving a common problem. The bigger the problem, the bigger the opportunity. I discovered a big one when I took apart an IBM PC. I made two interesting discoveries: The components were all manufactured by other companies, and the system that retailed for $3,000 cost about $600 in parts.”Michael Dell’s Powerful Lesson About Solving Problems and Building BusinessesThe quote highlights the importance of identifying inefficiencies and turning them into business opportunities. Dell explains that his breakthrough came from understanding the gap between manufacturing costs and retail pricing in the personal computer industry.By taking apart an IBM PC, Dell realized that many computer components were sourced from outside manufacturers and assembled into a final product sold at a significantly higher price. This observation helped shape his vision of creating a more direct and cost-efficient approach to selling computers.131281258Quote of the Day May 23: Why Great Business Ideas Often Begin With Everyday ProblemsThe quote also reflects a broader lesson in entrepreneurship: major business opportunities often emerge when people question existing systems instead of simply accepting them.The quote is about curiosity, problem-solving, and recognizing hidden opportunities. Dell suggests that successful entrepreneurs pay close attention to everyday frustrations, inefficiencies, and market gaps.His statement about the “bigger problem” creating a “bigger opportunity” reflects the idea that solving widespread challenges can lead to major innovation and business growth. Instead of focusing only on products, the quote emphasizes understanding systems, costs, and customer needs.131280035Who Is Michael DellMichael Dell is an American entrepreneur, businessman, and author best known as the founder and CEO of Dell Technologies, one of the world’s leading computer companies.Born on February 23, 1965, in Houston, Texas, Dell started building and selling customized computers from his dorm room while studying at the University of Texas at Austin. In 1984, he launched PCs Limited with $1,000 in start-up capital. By the middle of his freshman year, he had already sold $80,000 worth of computers. At age 19, he left college to run the business full-time, as per a Britannica report.Dell built his company around lower costs, faster delivery, and direct sales instead of relying heavily on retail stores. In 1992, he became the youngest CEO to lead a company onto Fortune magazine’s list of the top 500 corporations, as per the Britannica report.Over the years, Dell expanded the company beyond personal computers into software, services, and enterprise technology. In 2016, he became CEO of the newly formed parent company, Dell Technologies, following the acquisition of EMC.Beyond business, Dell and his wife, Susan, founded the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation in 1999 to support education, health, safety, and child-focused initiatives around the world.131268134Famous Quotes by Michael DellHere are a few more quotes by Michael Dell. You don't have to be a genius or a visionary or even a college graduate to be successful. You just need a framework and a dream, as per BrainyQuote. Buying a company that is number one in its business is hard to do. When something is for sale, it's often not a leader, as per BrainyQuote. You have to imagine a world in which there's this abundance of data, with all of these connected devices generating tons and tons of data. And you're able to reason over the data with new computer science and make your product and service better. What does your business look like then? That's the question every CEO should be asking, as per BrainyQuote. There are many different kinds of PCs. You have fixed, virtual, tablets, notebooks, ultrabooks, desktops, workstations. What you find in commercial PCs, business PCs, is that there's a really long tail of usage on client devices, as per BrainyQuote.131267379
items.snippet: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: Explore Michael Dell's insights on entrepreneurship and innovation, emphasizing the importance of identifying and solving common problems to create successful businesses. Learn from the founder of Dell Technologies about turning inefficiencies into opportunities.

items.headline: Easy picnic food ideas: Curate the perfect menu for easy-breezy summer outings
items.body: Good food, fresh air, and zero fuss. Here’s how to plan the perfect picnic with simple, stylish, and delicious ideas. (Photo: Pexels) Keep picnic simple with fruits, salads, breads, and small bites Grazing tables of breads, cheeses, olives, berries add flair Chilled drinks and light cocktails set the picnic mood Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan The first rule of picnic planning is simple — don’t overcomplicate it. Think juicy fruits, herby salads, soft breads, and small bites that don’t require reheating or too much handling. One can also set up a grazing table and make it fancy with charcuterie boards and platters. Start with a base of artisanal breads like sourdough, baguettes, or even soft focaccia. Add a mix of cheeses, keeping both soft and hard varieties for contrast. A handful of olives, some nuts, and fresh berries can bring in texture and colour without much effort. Layer in cut fruits like melon slices, grapes, or citrus wedges to keep the visual feel alive. Small sandwiches, mini sliders, or even neatly cut wraps work beautifully here. They’re filling without being messy and easy to pick up between conversations. Also Read: Pani puri conundrum and what to make of food cravings while fasting Add a few thoughtful mains While grazing is at the heart of a picnic, a couple of well-chosen dishes can give the spread more depth. Salads are the easiest way to do this and can be carried in a picnic basket with equal ease. A chilled pasta salad with herbs, a couscous mix with roasted vegetables, or even a simple citrus salad can add brightness and balance. These dishes travel well, hold their flavour, and don’t demand immediate serving. Mini quiches, savoury tarts, or bite-sized pastries are also ideal. They feel a little indulgent but remain practical as there are no knives, no fuss, just good food that works outdoors. Desserts at a picnic don’t need to be dramatic, but they should feel like a treat. The best options are those that are easy to serve and even easier to enjoy. Macarons, fruit tarts, lemon cakes, or chocolate-dipped strawberries strike that perfect balance. Drinks that set the mood No picnic feels complete without something refreshing to sip on. Drinks aren’t just about hydration but they set the tone for the entire experience. For daytime gatherings, chilled lemonade, iced tea, or fruit-infused sparkling water work beautifully. Serve them in glass bottles or simple dispensers with slices of citrus or sprigs of mint — it’s a small detail, but it makes a difference. Also Read: 5 delicious high-protein, no-LPG breakfast recipes shared by a nutritionist If the picnic stretches into the evening, light cocktails come into play. A crisp spritzer, a jug of sangria, or even a well-chilled rosé fits seamlessly into the relaxed setting. Add a garnish like a slice of orange or a fresh herb to give it a cute touch on a lazy sunny afternoon.
items.snippet: There’s something about a picnic that calls for a different kind of cooking which is less formal, more thoughtful. It isn’t about elaborate meals or perfectly plated courses. Instead, it’s about food that travels well, tastes fresh, and invites people to sit back, linger, and share

items.headline: Weeks-long ground offensive in Iran? What Pentagon's plans really mean and why Trump’s Kharg Island idea could backfire
items.body: A soldier stands guard on the deck of the US Navy Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Gridley (DDG 101), docked at the Amador cruise terminal in Panama City on March 29, 2026. (Photo by MARTIN BERNETTI / AFP) The US is preparing for possible sustained ground operations in Iran, with troop deployments and plans targeting strategic sites like Kharg Island. While no final decision is made, the buildup signals a shift from airstrikes amid concerns about escalation risks. Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan The United States is preparing for a potentially dramatic escalation in its conflict with Iran, with the Pentagon drawing up plans for sustained ground operations that could last weeks, according to several reports, including The Washington Post and Al Jazeera . What began as an air and naval campaign is now inching closer to a phase that could involve American troops operating on Iranian soil. While US officials continue to insist that no final decision has been taken, the scale of planning and troop movements suggests that Washington is seriously weighing the option. Pentagon planning signals shift from air war to boots on ground According to The Washington Post and Al Jazeera, the Pentagon has been tasked with preparing options for ground operations that would go beyond short-duration raids. These plans envision operations lasting several weeks, targeting specific high-value objectives rather than attempting a full-scale invasion of Iran. The planning includes the possible deployment of US Marines, Army units, and Special Operations forces, with a focus on rapid, high-impact missions. Officials quoted in the reports indicated that these operations could involve securing key sites, including coastal infrastructure and strategic assets linked to Iran’s military and energy network. Related Stories 'We control Iran's money': Trump says Tehran is 'playing tricks', warns US can strike with 'great fo... Mohsin Naqvi flies to Tehran for sixth time with a 'special message': Is Pakistan still relevant in ... Oil flows through Strait of Hormuz continue despite attacks as 12 tankers switch cargo The preparations are part of what US officials describe as contingency planning. As White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said, “It’s the job of the Pentagon to make preparations… It does not mean the president has made a decision.” However, the very nature of these preparations reflects growing concern within Washington that airstrikes alone may not be sufficient to achieve US objectives, particularly against hardened or underground targets. Troop deployments and regional build-up underline seriousness The planning is being backed by a visible build-up of US forces in the region. Reports indicate that thousands of troops are being positioned to provide operational flexibility if a decision is made to escalate. Thousands of US troops are already being positioned in the region: Around 3,500 Marines deployed aboard USS Tripoli Additional troops from the 82nd Airborne Division under consideration Total reinforcements could reach 10,000 personnel The US military assets including Marines deployed aboard amphibious assault ships, as well as airborne units, are being placed on standby. The scale of the deployment could rise into the thousands, creating the logistical backbone required for sustained operations. This buildup is not only about preparing for combat but also about deterrence and signalling. By placing troops within striking distance, the US is both increasing pressure on Iran and keeping multiple military options open. At the same time, officials remain cautious in public messaging, emphasising that these are preparatory steps rather than confirmed plans. Why Washington may be considering ground action The push towards ground operations is being driven by limitations of the current campaign. Despite extensive bombing, Iran’s core military capabilities, particularly its missile infrastructure and underground facilities, remain only partially degraded. Reports cited by Firstpost and Moneycontrol suggest that some targets, especially those buried deep underground or located within fortified complexes, may not be fully neutralised through airstrikes alone. This has led to discussions about the need for physical access to certain sites. Ground operations could also allow the US to secure strategic locations, disrupt Iran’s ability to project power in the Gulf, and potentially gain control over key nodes in its military and energy network. However, such a move would represent a significant escalation and a departure from the current strategy of remote warfare. Risks of escalation and Iranian retaliation Military experts warn that even limited ground operations in Iran carry enormous risks. Unlike previous US interventions in the region, Iran has significant conventional and asymmetric capabilities that could be brought to bear against invading forces. Iranian officials have already signalled that any ground incursion would be met with a strong response. The prospect of US troops operating inside Iran raises the likelihood of direct confrontation, prolonged engagement, and potentially heavy casualties. Beyond the battlefield, the repercussions could spread across the region. Iran could target US bases, disrupt shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, or escalate attacks through allied groups across the Middle East. The conflict could also trigger severe economic consequences, particularly in global energy markets, given the Gulf’s central role in oil supply. Trump’s Kharg Island plan: Seizing Iran’s oil lifeline At the centre of the debate over ground operations is Kharg Island, Iran’s most critical oil export hub and a focal point of US strategic thinking. Trump has openly suggested the possibility of seizing the island, framing it in stark economic terms. “My favourite thing is to take oil,” he said, hinting at the idea of capturing Iran’s energy infrastructure. Kharg Island handles the vast majority of Iran’s oil exports, making it one of the most valuable targets in the conflict. Capturing or disabling it would deal a major blow to Iran’s economy and significantly limit its ability to fund military operations. Pentagon planning reportedly includes scenarios involving amphibious assaults and rapid occupation of the island’s facilities. However, reports also highlight that such an operation would be extremely complex and risky. Iran is believed to have heavily fortified Kharg Island, anticipating that it could become a primary target. Any attempt to seize it would likely face stiff resistance and could quickly escalate into a broader confrontation. Experts have described the potential operation as “a suicide mission in the making,” reflecting concerns about the high costs and uncertain outcomes of such a move. A conflict at a turning point The Pentagon’s preparations mark a critical juncture in the war. While ground operations remain a contingency, the increasing focus on such plans suggests that the conflict is moving into a more dangerous and unpredictable phase. What is currently framed as limited, targeted action could easily expand, drawing the United States deeper into a prolonged conflict with Iran. With troop build-ups underway, strategic targets identified, and rhetoric around seizing key assets intensifying, the line between preparation and execution appears increasingly thin. The coming weeks may determine whether the conflict remains contained or escalates into a full-scale regional war with far-reaching global consequences.
items.snippet: US ground offensive in Iran? While US officials continue to insist that no final decision has been taken, the scale of planning and troop movements suggests that Washington is seriously weighing the option.

items.headline: The Moon is making your days longer, and most people have no idea
items.body: You probably haven’t noticed, but your days are getting longer. Not in the “I wish this workday would end” sense, but literally. The Earth is slowing down, and the Moon is applying the brakes. The numbers show it. Scientists have confirmed it. Here's the kicker: our own carbon footprint is now part of the equation.The Moon is drifting away, and taking our time with itEach year, the Moon moves about 1.5 inches (3.8 cm) farther away from Earth. That sounds like a little change, but that slow drift has had a huge impact on the length of our days over billions of years. In the early days of Earth, a full day was less than 13 hours in length. Now it’s 24, and still climbing.The reason boils down to tidal friction. As the Earth rotates, the Moon’s gravity pulls on the oceans, creating the familiar high and low tides along the coasts of places like Miami or Cape Cod. But there’s a delicate tug of war going on. The Earth spins faster than the Moon orbits, so the tidal bulge in the ocean gets pulled a little ahead of the Moon. That misalignment acts as a brake on the spin of our planet, transferring energy to the Moon and nudging it into a slightly higher orbit year after year.131259967A peer-reviewed study posted on arXiv, which analyzed centuries of lunar laser ranging data and eclipse records, found that Earth’s day has been getting longer by approximately 1.09 milliseconds per century since the late 1600s. Some estimates, based on ancient eclipse observations, put it even higher, at 1.78 milliseconds per century. It may seem like nothing, but, compounded over the 4.5 billion years of Earth’s history, that is everything.Why your phone clock might eventually need fixing Here is where things start to look surprisingly modern. The same climate change that’s producing record-breaking summers across the American South and melting glaciers in Alaska is now measurably affecting how fast the Earth spins. All that water is moving towards the planet's equator, making Earth's waistline a little bigger as ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica melt.In a landmark study published in Nature, geophysicist Duncan Agnew of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego found that melting polar ice is slowing Earth’s rotation just enough to affect global timekeeping. Atomic clocks, the same systems that synchronize your smartphone, GPS and financial transactions, are calibrated to Earth’s rotation. The planet has actually been spinning a little faster in recent decades due to changes in its liquid outer core, and for the first time in history, scientists were preparing to wipe a “negative leap second” from global clocks. Agnew's research indicated that ice melt from climate change has delayed that unprecedented step by about three years, putting it around 2028.131260043 Things are happening that are unprecedented, Agnew said. It's staggering to think that human activity could, by any measure, measurably change the rotation speed of an entire planet.The Atlantic Ocean is secretly supercharging the tidesThere’s another crazy twist to the story. The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth is not constant; it varies with the shape of the oceans. We're in a very high-drag period right now, and part of that is the North Atlantic.The present shape and size of the North Atlantic basin create a natural resonance; the water sloshes back and forth with a frequency that almost matches the tides. The net effect is that tides today are significantly bigger than they would be otherwise. It’s like giving a kid a push on a swing at the right moment; the timing magnifies the motion. This resonance will die away and then recur in different forms as the continents drift, for millions of years to come.131260156What this means for the rest of usNone of this will impact your morning commute. Changes to Earth’s rotation are so slow that they are measured in milliseconds per century. But zoom out far enough, and the picture is humbling. The Moon shaped the very rhythm of life on this planet, the length of our days, the force of our tides, perhaps even the origin of life itself.The Moon has been slowing the Earth down for 4.5 billion years. It took humanity a few decades to get in on it.
items.snippet: Explore the surprising link between the Moon's movement and Earth's slowing rotation, and how climate change is impacting our day length. Discover the science behind tidal friction and its effect on timekeeping.

items.headline: Govt AGR relief, fresh funding fuel 61% rally in Vodafone Idea stock since April
items.body: ET Intelligence Group: The stock of Vodafone Idea (VIL) has gained 61% since the beginning of April, hitting a 52-week high on Thursday. It has been scaling peaks, buoyed by the government's relief on dues pertaining to adjusted gross revenue (AGR), fresh promoter funding and potential debt funding by banks. Operational performance has also shown early signs of stabilisation, with narrowing losses, higher average revenue per user (ARPU), and reduced subscriber churn, supported by a credit rating upgrade to 'positive' from 'stable' by ICRA. Despite these positives, long-term performance hinges on VIL's ability to rebuild its subscriber base, sustain ARPU growth, secure further funding, and navigate competitive intensity in the telecom sector. The fund infusion of ₹4,730 crore by Aditya Birla group, one of the promoters, taking its stake to around 13% from 9.6%, has strengthened funding visibility by reviving hopes of a further funding by banks and finance companies. This follows the government's revision of AGR liabilities to ₹64,046 crore from ₹87,695 crore and a favourable repayment structure, including a five-year moratorium, which will ease near-term cash flow pressures.131254510 A similar fund-raise in 2024 had failed to unlock bank financing due to uncertainty over AGR dues, but the latest clarity could change lender stance. In May 2024, the Birla group infused ₹2,075 crore while ₹18,000 crore were raised through a follow-on offer (FPO) to augment 4G presence and to deploy 5G services. Apart from funding, the second crucial factor is the turnaround in VIL's operating parameters. Its subscriber base has shrunk significantly with its share in total user base falling to 12.1% in FY26 from 14.8% in FY23. Also, the number of active users fell to 169.3 million from 207.9 million during the period. On the positive side, average revenue per user (ARPU) rose to ₹190 from ₹135 between FY23 and FY26, aided by a slew of tariff increases. In addition, even though its subscriber base shrank, the average 4G/5G data usage increased to 20.2 GB from 15.5 GB during the said period. The other factor to watch is competitive intensity in the domestic sector, which has been rationalised over the past few years as incumbents tend to raise tariffs in tandem. Strategies used by VIL to grow the user base and data penetration will determine whether the sector reports yet another bout of high competitive intensity.
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea shares are soaring, hitting a 52-week high. Government relief on dues and promoter funding are boosting the stock. Operational improvements show narrowing losses and rising average revenue per user. The company is working to rebuild its subscriber base and navigate a competitive market. This positive momentum offers hope for future growth and stability.

items.headline: Pre-approved loans sound easy. They’re not always a good idea
items.body: Representative image Pre-approved loans fuel impulse borrowing, not real needs Convenience can lead to overlooking loan terms and higher costs Easy credit habits may impact long-term financial discipline Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Pre-approved loans are designed to feel effortless. You receive a message saying you are eligible for a certain amount, the process is minimal, and the money can reach your account almost instantly. On the surface, it feels less like borrowing and more like access to funds you already “qualify” for. That framing is powerful, and that’s exactly why it needs a closer look. The shift from need-based borrowing to impulse borrowing Most people take loans when there is a clear need. It could be a medical emergency, a large purchase, or a planned expense. The process involves some level of thought, comparison and decision-making. Pre-approved loans change that sequence. The offer comes first, and the need often gets created afterwards. What starts as curiosity, “I’m eligible, maybe I should use it”, can quickly turn into a financial commitment that was never really necessary in the first place. Related Stories Should you take a low-interest pre-approved loan or apply for a fresh loan? Pre-approved loans: Why banks offer them and what to check before accepting Should you opt for a low-interest pre-approved loan or a fresh loan? This shift, from need-based borrowing to impulse borrowing, is where many people begin to lose control over their debt. Convenience comes at the cost of scrutiny The biggest selling point of pre-approved loans is speed. The lender offers minimal documentation, quick approvals and fast disbursal, which makes the loan highly attractive. In this hurry, many people don’t pause to think about, say, comparing interest rates, checking the terms of the loan, additional charges etc. In fact, most people even forget to negotiate. It's almost like the offer is already sitting in your account or app, and all you want to say is yes before it disappears. Pre-approved doesn’t mean it’s the best deal There’s a natural assumption that if a bank has pre-approved a loan for you, it must be offering you a good rate. That’s not necessarily true. All it really means is that you fit their lending criteria. The pricing is about convenience, not generosity. If you take the time to compare, you might find better rates or more flexible terms elsewhere. And over a few years, even a small difference in interest can add up to a noticeable extra cost. The slow squeeze on your monthly cash flow At the time you take the loan, the EMI rarely feels like a big deal. It’s just another number that seems manageable. But that EMI doesn’t go away. It shows up every month, quietly eating into your income. Then another loan comes along, and another EMI gets added. Over time, what looked manageable in isolation starts to feel restrictive. You have less room to save, invest or handle unexpected expenses. It’s rarely one big decision that causes stress. It’s the build-up of several small ones. It can affect your bigger financial plans Every loan you take becomes part of your financial profile. When you apply for something more important, like a home loan, lenders look at your total obligations, not just your salary or credit score. So that pre-approved loan you took casually can end up reducing how much you’re eligible to borrow later, or affect the terms you’re offered. A short-term decision, made for convenience, can start shaping long-term outcomes. The habit it quietly creates There’s also a behavioural side to this that doesn’t get talked about enough. Once you get used to easy credit, it becomes the default solution. Instead of saving up for something, you start borrowing for it. Then doing it again becomes easier. Over time, that shift matters. It moves you away from building financial discipline and towards depending on credit. When it actually makes sense To be fair, pre-approved loans are not always a bad idea. There are situations where speed matters, when you need money quickly and don’t have the time or bandwidth to go through a longer process. In those cases, the convenience is real and useful. But even then, it’s worth pausing long enough to understand what you’re signing up for. The bottom line A pre-approved loan is just an offer. It’s not advice, and it’s not a signal that you should borrow. The decision still needs the same level of thought as any other loan. Once you take it, the ease of access disappears, but the repayment stays with you every month.
items.snippet: They look like easy money, but the real cost often shows up much later.

items.headline: NASA's Artemis II crew to wear "smart bands" on Moon mission—But is this a good idea?
items.body: Artemis II astronauts will wear smartwatch to track their physical and mental state. (Representative Image: Canva) NASA to equip Artemis II astronauts with smart wearable bands. Bands will monitor sleep, stress, and cognition in deep space. Artemis II to send 4 astronauts around Moon on April 1, 2026. Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan As NASA prepares for its next big leap with Artemis II. The space agency is sending something unexpected to deep space: smart wearable bands. Astronauts will wear these bands during their journey. This has given rise to an important question, is sending smart wearable bands to deep space a good idea? Smart Wristbands for Space Survival These smart bands are a part of a research project called ARCHeR, or Artemis Research for Crew Health and Readiness. Unlike regular smart bands, which are used to monitor fitness, these smart bands are meant to work in space. It will continuously record key human metrics, which will provide us with unprecedented insights into the well-being of our astronauts. What NASA is trying to measure? Related Stories ISRO joins NASA’s Moon Programme: Can India outpace China in the moon race? Here’s what to know Solar Eclipse 2026: Moon will cover 96% of the Sun and create the UK’s deepest eclipse since 1999 Solar Eclipse 2026: At what time the event begins and will 'India' see it? Know everything here The smart bands will measure sleep patterns, which are affected by space conditions. They will also measure stress and fatigue levels, as well as physical movements. Smart bands will also measure mental performance and decision-making skills of astronauts. Unlike regular smart bands, which are used to monitor fitness, these smart bands will try to decode human behavior when pushed beyond normal conditions. Why is this more important than it appears? Not only is space in deep space physically demanding, but it is also psychologically demanding. There is no day-night cycle, and there is no personal space. The astronauts are under constant pressure. NASA needs real-time data to determine if astronauts are sharp, stable, and synchronized during space travel. Artemis II: A crucial test mission Artemis II is one of the most significant milestones in the history of space exploration. The mission will involve sending astronauts to the Moon. The mission is planned to last for 10 days. NASA is scheduled to launch the mission on 6:24 PM EDT on April 1, 2026. The mission will involve sending 4 astronauts to space. The mission will be launched from Earth. The mission is significant because it will be the first time humanity will be going back to deep space after more than 50 years since the Apollo program.
items.snippet: NASA will send smartbands with Artemis II astronauts to track their physical and mental state. But whether this helps or complicates deep-space survival remains an open question.

items.headline: Textile wall art ideas are trending in Indian homes, here's how to style them easily
items.body: How to decorate walls: Materials like resham, kasab, beads and cords each bring a distinct identity to wall art. Together, they create something that feels both contemporary and deeply rooted (Images: V V. Exports Universal Pvt. Ltd) Textile wall art brings warmth and texture to modern interiors Regional embroidery and weaving add cultural richness to spaces Mixed media textiles craft expressive, layered visual narratives Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan There was a time when walls of your rooms spoke only through paint and canvas. Today, the trend is to decorate the walls with threads, fabric, and handwork. Like fashion, art has moved with the times. What was once confined to brushstrokes has now found expression in textiles. Designers are exploring beyond the obvious, guided as much by instinct as by tradition. “Artists today are constantly trying to create something unique while preserving the integrity of artistic expression,” Kailash Poojary, Founder and CEO of V V. Exports Universal Pvt. Ltd, tells Moneycontrol . “Textile-based wall art offers that freedom to reinvent,” he adds. India’s long-standing textile heritage plays a powerful role in this shift. From regional embroidery to time-honoured weaving, the craft vocabulary is vast. What is new, however, is how it is being used. Minimal homes are now punctuated with a single striking piece. Empty walls are giving way to curated spaces where one artwork that is rich in texture takes centre stage, reflecting your personality. Also read | How to create statement walls that make your living room look rich and luxurious There is a certain warmth in fabric that paint rarely achieves. The layered surfaces, the play of threads, the gentle irregularity of handwork, these details make textile art feel alive. “Materials like resham, kasab, beads and cords each bring a distinct identity. Together, they create something that feels both contemporary and deeply rooted,” Poojary says. As homes become more personal, the shift towards textile wall art feels almost inevitable. It is not merely decoration, it is expression. And in every thread, there is both memory and modernity, quietly stitched together. How to decorate your walls Poojari shares ways to decorate your wall with these textile techniques. Regional embroidery techniques Traditional embroidery brings colour and cultural richness into a room without overwhelming it. Framed fabric pieces work well in living rooms or hallways, adding a sense of heritage while still fitting neatly into modern interiors. Also read | 5 Vastu-approved paintings to hang on your home walls Time-honoured weaving practices Handwoven textiles offer an earthy charm. Used as wall panels in bedrooms or reading corners, they soften the space and introduce texture, creating an atmosphere that feels calm, grounded, and comfortably lived-in. Aari work Known for its fine detailing, Aari embroidery suits spaces where subtle elegance matters. A framed Aari piece above a bed or console invites closer attention, rewarding the viewer with its delicate, almost meditative craftsmanship. Zardozi work Zardozi, with its metallic threads and rich embellishments, lends a sense of occasion to interiors. Placed against a neutral wall, it becomes an immediate focal point; bold, refined, and luxurious without being excessive. Macramé Macramé introduces a relaxed, contemporary touch. Hung near windows or balconies, its knotted patterns interact beautifully with natural light, adding softness and movement to spaces that might otherwise feel too structured or rigid. Mixed material textile art By combining threads, beads, and fabrics, mixed media pieces create depth and variety. A small gallery wall using such artworks can feel personal and expressive, turning an ordinary wall into a layered visual story.
items.snippet: Textile wall art is reshaping modern Indian homes, blending tradition with contemporary style. From embroidery to macramé, designers are turning to fabric-based art to add warmth, texture, and personality to minimal spaces.

items.headline: In the 1950s, one stubborn chemical spill at a 3M lab sparked the idea behind Scotchgard
items.body: Scotchgard started with an accidental spill that acted unusually in a laboratory. In the early postwar period, scientists at 3M were experimenting with fluorochemical compounds, which were supposed to resist water and oil. In those days, many companies competed for inventing new materials to enhance various products in industry and daily life. But then something extraordinary occurred in the lab.A chemical spill fell on a shoe and on some fabric. The fabric was not stained by the liquid, as it usually happens. It rather repelled it. This property of the compound seemed to be promising from a commercial point of view. This observation became one of the reasons why a stain-resistant fabric protector, Scotchgard, was developed. What is more interesting about the story is the combination of an accident, chemistry, and usefulness.Post-war boom in the chemistry of fluorochemicalsScotchgard story took place against the background of the fast development of fluorochemical chemistry. According to a review published in PubMed, PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances), a group of thousands of synthetic forever chemicals , gained importance commercially starting in the 1950s, with companies such as 3M spearheading their production and experiments.It was the quest of scientists to find products that could repel oil, grease, and water. The properties were particularly interesting for textiles and other industrial uses. This is when 3M obtained fluorochemical technology as early as 1947 and started commercializing its development by 1952.This background information was crucial because scientists were already investigating substances capable of changing the surface's characteristics.What made the spill specialLab accidents are common occurrences, yet most of them go unnoticed. The spill became significant because of the unique reaction of the chemical used. The liquid droplets formed beads rather than absorbing into the surface. The peculiar reaction turned what could have been just another spill into a potential product.Scientists realized that people would appreciate clothing, carpets, and furniture items that could resist spills and stains. The chemistry responsible for the phenomenon came down to fluorinated products. According to a PubMed Central review of PFOS compounds, the widespread use of these chemicals in surface treatments could be attributed to their properties to repel liquids and avoid contamination.131223680How Scotchgard became a consumer productCommercialization of the discovery involved many years of experiments and developments. 3M developed the technology to apply fluorochemical coatings to fabrics without ruining the texture and appearance of the material. The timing made it possible for the product to succeed.In the 1950s, American families started using products designed for convenience, such as easy-to-clean fabrics and household cleaning solutions. Companies competed to simplify people's lives through convenient products. Scotchgard came right at the right time.The product offered protection against spills to furniture, carpets, and clothing without altering the appearance of the materials. Scientific research suggests that this trend made products such as Scotchgard popular during the post-war economic boom.Environmental risks behind Scotchgard’s success storyDespite the commercial success of Scotchgard, the chemicals behind the stain resistance technology attracted increasing scientific and environmental concerns. According to a study in PubMed Central, 3M made a voluntary decision to stop producing PFOS and other such chemicals from 2000 to 2002 due to their persistence in the environment and potential adverse effects on health.This fact significantly influenced the perception of fluorochemical products by many people. Researchers who were studying PFAS chemicals noticed that some substances stayed in the environment for a long time and had the ability to accumulate there. Thus, the story behind Scotchgard became rather complicated and was not just an example of an innovative product.What seemed initially to be a consumer breakthrough turned into a bigger discussion of industrial chemicals, their safety, and environmental issues. The incident illustrates the importance of timing and context. The oil spill by itself was not sufficient. Scientists required both the scientific knowledge, manufacturing technology, and consumer demand for converting the incident into a successful product.Simultaneously, the history of Scotchgard adds another dimension of caution in its own right. The very chemical characteristics that made it useful for stain resistance posed serious environmental problems many years later. Innovation coupled with consequences makes the story contemporary even today.
items.snippet: An accidental lab spill in the 1950s led to the creation of Scotchgard, a revolutionary stain-repellent fabric protector.  Developed by 3M amidst a boom in fluorochemical research, the product offered convenience to post-war consumers. However, the very chemicals that made it effective later raised significant environmental and health concerns, highlighting the complex legacy of industrial innovation.

items.headline: Festive Fashion 2026: Easy, breathable outfit ideas for Navratri, Eid and Gudi Padwa
items.body: Festive season + summer heat? Here’s how to stay stylish and comfortable. Think mulmul saris, breezy florals, and effortless fusion looks. (Photos: Pinterest) Festive wardrobes focus on comfort, breathable fabrics, and ease White outfits and florals trend for festival celebrations Mixing existing pieces creates fresh, modern festive looks Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan This weekend arrives with a certain kind of momentum and we can’t help but love it. The holy festivals of Chaitra Navratri, Gudi Padwa, Ugadi, and Eid-ul-Fitr line up almost back-to-back, bringing with them a mix of early morning rituals, long lunches, evening gatherings, and the inevitable wardrobe dilemma. It’s not just about what looks good but what holds up through the day, especially when the heat refuses to take a day off. The smartest festive wardrobes this season aren’t about excess. They’re about ease, movement, and pieces that transition without demanding a full outfit change. Think fabrics that breathe, silhouettes that don’t restrict, and styling that feels considered but never overdone. Also Read: Eid ul-Fitr 2026 fashion: Get ready for festive celebrations in vibrant shararas pathani suits and vintage saree makeovers Here are five ways to get it right All white, but far from basic There’s something about an all-white outfit that instantly feels festive, even without heavy embellishment. This year, it’s less about stark whites and more about softer, nuanced tones — what designers are calling the “cloud dancer” palette. Salwar kurta sets, shararas, and co-ord sets in tone-on-tone embroidery keep things interesting without feeling loud. The trick lies in texture and fabrics like chikankari, subtle threadwork, or layered fabrics that catch light just enough. Finish the look with juttis or Kolhapuris and a pair of chandbalis. It’s classic, but it doesn’t feel dated. Florals that don’t try too hard Floral styles for festive wear aren’t new, but the way they’re showing up this season feels lighter, almost more personal. Linen and cotton take centre stage, especially in pieces like breezy salwar suits, lehengas, and floor-length anarkalis. Hand-painted botanical prints add certain softness and you can tell when something hasn’t come straight off a machine. Keep the rest of the styling simple with sleek gold jewellery, neutral footwear, and let the outfit do the talking. Let it flow There’s no reason festive dressing should feel restrictive, especially in this weather. Free-flowing silhouettes are having a moment, and rightly so. Silk kaftans, loose satin shirts paired with matching trousers, and lehariya skirts worn with easy kurtas strike that balance between comfort and presence. These are outfits you can sit in for hours, move around in, and still look put together. Mulmul saris, always If there’s one piece that truly understands the Indian summer, it’s the mulmul sari . Light, breathable, and endlessly elegant, it works across occasions without much effort. The beauty of it lies in how you style it. A well-cut blouse with an unexpected but respectful neckline or sleeve detail can completely change the mood. Add stacks of colourful bangles, maybe a few fresh flowers in your hair, and you have a look that feels rooted yet fresh. Also Read: Velvet, the winter fabric that owns festive fashion in India, is back in vogue A little fusion never hurts Festive wardrobes don’t need to stay within strict lines anymore. Mixing pieces you already own can often lead to the most interesting looks. A sari paired with a trench-style baroque jacket for the evening, or a crisp white shirt worn with a handcrafted waistcoat and dhoti pants. These creative combinations feel current without trying too hard. It’s less about buying something new and more about seeing your existing wardrobe differently.
items.snippet: You’re dressing for long days, multiple settings, and moments that matter. The best outfits are the ones that move with you — quietly doing their job, while you focus on everything celebratory

items.headline: Driving at 75 mph burns 27% more fuel and most drivers have no idea
items.body: Let's be honest. No one likes to stand at the gas pump and watch the dollars spin like a slot machine. With fuel prices taking a serious bite out of your paycheck, second only to your car payment or lease, wringing every mile out of every gallon isn't just smart, it's a necessity.Here’s something most drivers don’t know. The speed you drive has a dramatic effect on the amount of fuel you burn, and if you’re regularly cruising at 75 mph on the highway, which is pretty standard on an American interstate, you’re silently torching your gas money without even knowing it.The sweet spot most of us blow byThere's an optimum speed range for efficiency in your car. A study of 74 different vehicles by the Oak Ridge National Laboratory found the sweet spot to be between 40 and 50 mph. Once you get above 50 mph, your fuel economy starts to fall, and fall fast. At 80 mph, you are consuming approximately 27% more fuel than you would at 60 mph.Think about that in dollars. If your car gets 32 mpg at highway speeds and you fill up every week, that inefficiency adds up to hundreds of dollars a year, money that could go towards a car insurance payment, a weekend trip, or just some breathing room in a tight month.Here's how the Department of Energy puts it: for every 5 mph you drive over 50 mph, it's like paying an extra $.28 per gallon for gas. You wouldn't ignore a 28-cent increase at the pump. So why do we ignore the speed that does it?So why does speed hurt fuel economy so badly?The short answer: air hates you if you go fast.131222085The longer answer is that there is something called aerodynamic drag. This is the resistance your car experiences as it pushes through the air. At low speed, the resistance is okay, but as you accelerate, physics changes dramatically. Drag is not linear with speed. It rises with the square of your speed. So when you go from 45mph to 75mph, you are not just going 1.7 times faster, you are fighting roughly 2.8 times as much air resistance.A review of research published through the USC Viterbi School of Engineering reveals that aerodynamic forces affect fuel consumption more at highway speeds than at lower speeds, and the faster you go, the more pronounced the effects. At high speeds, aerodynamic drag can account for nearly half of your car’s overall fuel consumption.Your engine, then, works overtime. This takes more gas to maintain that speed against the increasing wall of air resistance. The faster you go, the more this happens, exponentially.What this means for your wallet right nowYou don't have to drive like it's a Sunday country cruise to make a difference. Small things matter.Slowing down from 75 mph to 65 mph on your everyday commute or road trip can greatly affect your fuel economy. On flat highways, keep a steady speed with cruise control; erratic acceleration is another silent gas waster. If you’re piling a rooftop cargo box on your car, know that it can cut your highway fuel economy by as much as 25%.None of this requires a new car, a hybrid, or a lifestyle overhaul. It just requires understanding what's happening under the hood and under the laws of physics, every time you put that accelerator towards 80.Gas prices may be out of your control. Your right foot isn't.
items.snippet: Discover how speeding at 75 mph dramatically increases fuel costs by 27%. Learn efficient driving tips and fuel economy tricks to save money at the pump.

items.headline: Dhurandhar 2 ending explained: Transformation of Ranveer Singh’s character Hamza could form core idea for next installment
items.body: Ranveer Singh in Dhurandhar 2 Ranveer Singh's character undergoes emotional change and separation. Film ends Pakistan chapter, but family ties remain unresolved Teases third film on internal conflict and personal stakes Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’ works both as a continuation and a closure, carefully tying up the loose ends left behind in the first film while still leaving the door open for what comes next. The story answers many of the lingering questions around Ranveer Singh’s character, but it does so without making things too neat or predictable. Towards the climax, there is a clear shift in tone. We see Ranveer Singh ’s character meeting Ajay Sanyal and Sushant Bansal, where he is asked to be ready for a debrief. The plan seems straightforward—Bansal will pick him up the next morning. But things take an unexpected turn. Instead of following orders, he quietly disappears and boards a train to Pathankot, his hometown. This moment stands out because it is not driven by action but by emotion and silence. Also Read: Dhurandhar 2 box office collection live updates: Allu Arjun, Preity Zinta, Vijay Deverakonda and other celebs laud Aditya Dhar, Ranveer Singh after watching preview shows At the railway station and later near his home, he watches his family from a distance. He does not meet them. He does not speak. And then, just when it feels like he might return to his old life, he makes a sudden u-turn. This single decision says a lot about who he has become. The man we saw earlier, someone emotional and deeply attached to his family, now feels distant and changed. This transformation could be the core idea for the next installment. This is not just a revenge story anymore; it is about the cost of living a double life for years. The fifteen-year-long mission has clearly left deep psychological scars on him. By the end, it becomes clear that while the external mission may be over, the internal conflict is far from resolved. The film also hints that the Pakistan chapter of his life is largely closed. Most of his targets are gone, and there is no strong reason for him to return. However, two important connections remain—his wife Yalina and their son. This emotional thread feels unfinished and could easily become the backbone of a third film. Another important track is Jameel Jamali, who once again shifts his political stance and becomes part of the ruling setup. With Yalina linking these worlds, there is scope for a layered subplot involving politics and personal history. In the end, the film leaves us at a crossroads. It is less about what he will do next and more about who he has become. If a third part happens, it is likely to explore his inner battles rather than just external missions, making the story more personal and intense.
items.snippet: Dhurandhar 2's story answers many of the lingering questions around Ranveer Singh’s character, but it does so without making things too neat or predictable.
