items.headline: Republic Day 2026: Speech and Essay Ideas with Samples in English for Students
items.body: Republic Day marks the adoption of India's Constitution on 26 January 1950 Schools and colleges host speeches, essays, and cultural events to celebrate the day. Students urged to uphold constitutional values and contribute to society Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Republic Day is observed every year on 26 January to mark the day when the Constitution of India came into force in 1950. The day holds great importance as it signifies India’s journey as a sovereign, democratic republic. Across the country, schools and colleges organise activities such as speech competitions, essay writing, debates and cultural programmes to help students understand the value of this historic day. Here are some simple and useful speech and essay ideas for Republic Day 2026. Republic Day 2026 Sample Speech Good morning respected teachers and my dear friends. Today, we are gathered here to celebrate Republic Day, one of the most important days in India’s history. On 26 January 1950, our country adopted its Constitution and became a republic. This day reminds us of the values of democracy, equality and justice. The Indian Constitution gives us fundamental rights and also reminds us of our duties as citizens. It allows us to live with freedom while respecting the law and one another. Republic Day is also a time to remember the sacrifices made by freedom fighters who worked hard to give us an independent nation. As we watch the Republic Day parade and take part in celebrations, we should promise to follow the ideals of the Constitution in our daily lives. Let us work together to make India stronger and more united. Thank you. Republic Day 2026 Speech Ideas 1. Republic Day and the Power of Ordinary Citizens This speech can focus on how the strength of India’s republic does not lie only in leaders or institutions, but in everyday citizens. Students can talk about how small actions like voting responsibly, following laws, and respecting public property keep democracy alive. 2. How the Constitution Shapes Our Daily Life Instead of discussing the Constitution in theory, this topic explains how it affects real life. Students can mention freedom of speech, equality in schools, and protection of rights, showing how the Constitution quietly guides everyday decisions. 3. Republic Day Beyond the Parade This speech can go beyond the usual discussion of parades and ceremonies. Students can explain why Republic Day is not just a celebration but a reminder to reflect on justice, fairness, and how well we follow constitutional values as a society. 4. The Role of Youth in Protecting Democracy This topic highlights the responsibility of young people in a republic. Students can speak about being informed, questioning misinformation, respecting differences, and using education as a tool to strengthen democracy. 5. Republic Day and India’s Diversity This speech can focus on how India’s Constitution respects languages, cultures, and traditions. Students can explain how unity does not mean sameness and why accepting diversity is essential for a democratic nation. Republic Day 2026 Sample Essay Republic Day: Upholding the Spirit of the Constitution Republic Day is celebrated on 26 January every year to honour the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1950. On this day, India officially became a democratic republic, replacing the colonial system of governance. The Constitution of India lays down the framework for the country’s political system and protects the rights of its citizens. Dr B.R. Ambedkar, along with members of the Constituent Assembly, played a key role in drafting the Constitution. It ensures equality, freedom and justice for all. Republic Day celebrations include a grand parade in New Delhi, showcasing India’s cultural diversity and military strength. For students, Republic Day is a reminder of their responsibility towards the nation. It encourages young citizens to respect the Constitution and contribute positively to society through honesty, hard work and unity. Republic Day 2026 Essay Ideas 1. Republic Day as a Reminder of Our Duties This essay can explore how Republic Day is often linked to rights, but duties are equally important. Students can discuss responsibilities such as obeying laws, respecting national symbols, and contributing positively to society. 2. The Constitution as a Living Document Instead of calling the Constitution a historical text, this essay can explain how it continues to evolve through amendments and court interpretations. Students can reflect on why flexibility is important in a changing society. 3. Republic Day and Social Equality in India This topic allows students to discuss how the Constitution aims to reduce inequality. The essay can talk about equal opportunities, reservations, and laws that protect marginalised groups, while also reflecting on the work still needed. 4. Why Republic Day Matters to Students Today This essay can connect Republic Day to student life. It can explain how education, freedom of thought, and equal access to opportunities are outcomes of constitutional values that directly benefit young citizens. 5. Republic Day as a Lesson in Nation Building Students can write about how Republic Day teaches patience, unity, and cooperation. The essay can focus on how nation building is a long process that requires effort from every generation, not just past leaders.
items.snippet: Here are simple speech and essay ideas for Republic Day 2026, to help students understand the importance of the Constitution, democracy and their role as responsible citizens.

items.headline: Quote of the Day by Lisa Kleypas: ‘I no longer believed in the idea of soul mates, or love at first sight,
items.body: In The Godfather, while hiding in Sicily, Michael Corleone sees Apollonia Vitelli for the first time and is struck by what locals call golpe di fulmine, the thunderbolt of love at first sight. Remembering the move makes sense, as it is sudden, intense, and impossible to ignore. Cinema and audiences love these grand amours, where love arrives like lightning and changes everything in an instant.But real life is often quieter for most in these matters. Not every great love begins with fireworks or fate. Sometimes, it grows slowly, through understanding, patience, and the comfort of being truly seen. If you are one of the unlucky bunches who failed to find love at first sight, without leaving you abandoned in your own cocoon of thought, author Lisa Kleypas can give you hope; the rest is up to you to find out.Quote of the Day by Lisa Kleypas: “I no longer believed in the idea of soul mates, or love at first sight. But I was beginning to believe that a very few times in your life, if you were lucky, you might meet someone who was exactly right for you. Not because he was perfect, or because you were, but because your combined flaws were arranged in a way that allowed two separate beings to hinge together.”Also Read: Quote of the Day by Bohdi Sanders: ‘Focus on making yourself better, not on thinking…’ - The secret mantra to becoming a better version of yourselfWhy Lisa Kleypas’s quote on love matters todayQuoted by Goodreads from her novel Blue-Eyed Devil, this love quote may read simple but to assimilate it might require multiple readings. Dating apps, fast attraction, and the lustrous idea of romance on social media may give you the pressure to find “the one” instantly, but fear not, as she believes that it's all messier than it looks.Lisa Kleypas’s quote matters because it shifts the focus from perfection and the beautification of romance to compatibility. It reminds readers that love is not about finding someone flawless; it is about finding someone who understands your flaws and stays anyway. That idea will feel more realistic and comforting to the people who are on the brink of being lost.Also Read: Quote of the Day by William the conqueror: ‘A faithless wife brings ruin to the state’ - What it’s about and the obscure lesson hidden behind this medieval warningWhat Lisa Kleypas’s quote means in real lifeThe quote speaks about emotional maturity. It suggests that love grows stronger when people stop chasing fantasy and start accepting reality. Instead of searching for a perfect partner, people begin looking for emotional safety, trust, and mutual understanding.In real life, the strongest relationships often happen this way. Two imperfect people meet, learn each other’s weaknesses, and still choose to stay. That choice creates a deeper bond than any fairy-tale version of love ever could.Also Read: Quote of the Day by Melody Carstairs: ‘If you’ve got nothing to dance about, find a reason to sing’ - The secret to staying hopeful in difficult timesWho is Lisa Kleypas?Lisa Kleypas is a bestselling American author best known for her romance and historical fiction novels. She graduated from Wellesley College with a degree in political science and later became one of the most recognized names in contemporary romance writing.Her books have been translated into forty different languages and have found readers across the world, as per her website. She lives in California with her husband, Gregory. Her upcoming novel, Queen of Lombard Street, is a new historical fiction release scheduled for October 20, 2026.
items.snippet: Quote of the Day by Lisa Kleypas: While cinema often portrays love at first sight, author Lisa Kleypas offers a more realistic perspective. Her quote emphasizes that true connection lies not in perfection, but in finding someone whose flaws complement yours, fostering a deeper, more enduring bond through mutual understanding and acceptance.

items.headline: Shiv Sena (UBT) is not just a party but an idea; BJP can't finish it: Uddhav Thackeray
items.body: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray Days after facing defeat in the Mumbai civic body polls, Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray has said that the BJP was mistaken if it thought it could finish his party, which was not just a political entity but an idea. Addressing party workers on Friday at an event organised as part of the birth centenary celebrations of late Bal Thackeray , his father and the founder of the undivided Shiv Sena, Uddhav said many people are trying to erase the Thackeray name, but it won't happen. His cousin and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray, who spoke before Uddhav, said the political situation in the state was like a "market of slaves" and referred to the civic body polls, including those in the Kalyan Dombivli Municipal Corporation, as an "auction" taking place in the state. "The BJP is wrong if it thinks it can finish Shiv Sena (UBT). The Shiv Sena (UBT) is not a party but an idea," Uddhav said. Had the Shiv Sena not been there, the BJP would have never seen the inside of the BMC or "Mantralaya" (the state government's headquarters), said the former chief minister. Related Stories Uddhav Thackeray to launch state-wide outreach campaign amid rebellion buzz in UBT Sena News live updates: Uddhav Thackeray calls key meeting of UBT legislators amid 'Operation Tiger' buzz Shiv Sena UBT rebel MPs likely to join Shinde-led Sena today: Report His remarks came after the BJP emerged as the single largest party in the January 15 polls to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), winning 89 seats in the 227-member House. In alliance with the Shiv Sena (29 seats) headed by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, the national party ended the Thackerays' decades-long control over India's richest civic body. The Shiv Sena (UBT)-Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) combine put up a better-than-expected fight in the BMC polls, but failed to stop the BJP-led Mahayuti from crossing the majority mark. The Sena (UBT) won 65 seats, while the MNS, led by Raj Thackeray, bagged 6. "They want to swallow Mumbai," Uddhav further said, adding that money power was used for the first time during the civic polls in the city. The BMC results may not be as per what the party desired, but the Opposition is a strong force in the civic body, he said. The Opposition faced several hurdles, such as flawed electoral rolls, and the result would have been even more different had the Sena (UBT) not identified dual voters, Uddhav said. "We have to start afresh," he said, adding that the Sena was born not for power but for fighting for the rights of Marathi manoos. He also said that attempts were afoot to impose non-Marathi culture on Maharashtra, and the decision (later revoked) to make Hindi compulsory in schools from Class 1 was part of this conspiracy. The slogan "Jai Maharashtra" — commonly used by Shiv Sena workers — was in danger, Uddhav said, and urged everyone to use it as a greeting. Raj said it was Bal Thackeray who proved that Hindus could be a political force, and even the BJP did not think that such a consolidation was possible.

items.headline: No Vodafone Idea-like AGR relief without court order, govt tells telcos
items.body: Airtel is unlikely to approach the courts in the immediate term, choosing instead to engage with the government directly, a Business Standard report says. Court order needed for telecom AGR dues relief, says Minister Scindia Vodafone Idea's AGR dues frozen; Airtel requests reassessment, no special concessions Vodafone Idea's revival seen as boosting competition in India's telecom sector Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Telecom operators seeking relief on adjusted gross revenue (AGR) arrears similar to the package extended to Vodafone Idea will first need a favourable court direction, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said, underlining that the government's decision in Vi's case was based strictly on a Supreme Court mandate, The Economic Times reported on Friday. Scindia told The Economic Times in an interview that while every stakeholder has the right to approach the judiciary, any relief from the government can only follow a court's directive. In Vodafone Idea's case, the Supreme Court had specifically asked the government to evaluate the company's request, which led to the relief package, he said, adding that the Centre also holds a 49% stake in the telecom operator. The government, he clarified, has no plans to raise that shareholding beyond the current level. The Economic Times had earlier reported that Bharti Airtel and Tata Group telecom units were weighing options to seek equitable treatment on AGR-linked statutory dues. Airtel chairman Sunil Mittal subsequently confirmed that the company has written to the government seeking a reassessment of its AGR liabilities, noting that the issue affected Airtel as well. However, Airtel is unlikely to approach the courts in the immediate term, choosing instead to engage with the government directly, Business Standard reported. Mittal, speaking from Davos on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum, said the company had sought a reassessment and recalculation of dues, describing the matter as one of mathematical correction rather than a legal dispute. Earlier this month, the government granted Vodafone Idea a significant reprieve by freezing its AGR dues at Rs 87,695 crore as of December 31, 2025, and allowing staggered repayments over 16 years until 2041. Under the revised schedule, Vi will pay Rs 124 crore annually for six years starting March 2026, followed by Rs 100 crore per year for the next four years. During this period, the company's AGR liabilities will be reassessed and finalised by a government-appointed committee, with repayments on the revised dues beginning in March 2036, as reported by both The Economic Times and Business Standard. Related Stories Vodafone Idea steps up capex as Rs 6,400 crore funding raised, lender talks advance Lightstorm raises Rs 2,500 crore debt from IndusInd bank to build fibre network connecting India’... Stocks to Watch Today: IRB Infra, Lupin, Bharat Electronics, Zen Tech, Lumax Auto, BSE, Wipro, PC Je... Airtel's AGR dues, by contrast, are estimated to exceed Rs 40,000 crore. The company has already paid around Rs 18,000 crore and had earlier sought conversion of part of its liabilities into equity. Since Airtel's dues have not been frozen, they continue to accrue, Business Standard noted. Mittal said Airtel was not seeking any special concessions but only a fair reassessment. If overpayments or double counting are corrected, he said, the principal amount would reduce, triggering a cascading drop in penalties and interest. Such an outcome, he argued, would ensure that the government collects only what is legitimately due. Scindia, meanwhile, reiterated that the Vodafone Idea relief does not automatically extend to other operators, and any similar request would have to follow the same legal route. He also told The Economic Times that the government has asked the Department of Telecommunications and the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India to examine the growing issue of spam shifting to over-the-top platforms, though OTT services do not directly fall under the telecom regulator's jurisdiction. On broader industry health, Mittal said Vodafone Idea's revival would strengthen competition in the Indian telecom market, which he believes can sustainably support three private operators alongside a state-owned player.
items.snippet: In Vodafone Idea's case, the Supreme Court had specifically asked the government to evaluate the company's request, which led to the relief package

items.headline: In big relief to Vodafone Idea, govt pares its AGR liabilities by 27%
items.body: Mumbai: The department of telecommunication (DoT) has cut Vodafone Idea's (Vi's) adjusted gross revenue (AGR) liabilities by nearly 27% in a major cash-flow relief that opens up avenues for fresh fundraising to the country's third-largest telecom operator.After reassessment of Vi's AGR dues, a DoT-appointed committee has finalised the total AGR amount at ₹64,046 crore as on December 31, 2025, Vi said in a regulatory filing on Thursday.Earlier, the DoT had frozen the AGR dues as on December 31 at ₹87,695 crore, subject to reassessment and final approval by the committee.130650786Following the reduction in Vi's AGR dues, rival Bharti Airtel may also again write to the DoT seeking reassessment of its AGR dues. The Sunil Mittal-led telco had earlier written to DoT seeking reassessment of its AGR dues but there was no action from DoT as it felt the company should get relief order from the Supreme Court.With the AGR dues now finalised, Vi will pay a minimum of ₹100 crore annually for four years between FY32 and FY35 under the approved payment schedule.The remaining dues will be settled in six equal annual instalments from FY36 to FY41, effectively freezing the bulk of the dues for a decade. The staggered repayments are now spread over 16 years, providing a much-needed breathing window to the struggling telco.Vi's shares closed 0.68% lower at ₹10.22 apiece on the BSE on Thursday, before the announcement was made late evening.The government has made several interventions to keep the struggling telecom operator afloat.Under its 2021 telecom relief package, the government offered a four-year moratorium to telcos, including Vi for payment of AGR and spectrum dues. The option to convert dues into equity was also given.In February 2023, nearly ₹16,000 crore of interest on VI's deferred spectrum and AGR dues was converted into equity, giving the government about 33% stake at the time. This was followed by the conversion of an additional ₹36,950 crore of spectrum auction dues into equity in April 2025, eventually raising its stake to 48.99%, making it the company's largest shareholder.
items.snippet: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has reduced Vodafone Ideas adjusted gross revenue (AGR) liabilities by about 27%, providing significant financial relief to the telecom operator.

items.headline: DoT trims Vodafone Idea AGR dues to Rs 64,046 crore, allows staggered payments
items.body: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has finalised the adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues of Vodafone Idea Limited at Rs 64,046 crore as of December 31, 2025, following directions from the Supreme Court of India to consider the company’s grievances, said Vi in a stock exchange filing on Thursday. The revised figure is lower than the earlier provisional estimate of Rs 87,695 crore.The DoT said the amount, assessed by a designated committee, will be paid in a staggered manner, with a minimum of Rs 100 crore annually over four years starting FY32, and the remaining dues to be cleared in six equal annual instalments from FY36 to FY41.The ⁠dues ⁠stem from a long legal dispute over government's method of calculating AGR, which telecom operators had contested as this metric determines ⁠licence fees ‌and other dues.Vi's shares closed 0.68% lower at ₹10.22 apiece on the BSE on Thursday.In December, the government approved a ⁠partial moratorium on Vi's dues, freezing them at Rs 87,695 crore and deferring repayments to the 2030s, providing near-term cash flow relief for the debt-saddled firm.The DoT's decision provides another respite to the telecom operator, which was facing a ₹16,400 crore payment due in March 2026. The company continues to grapple with a total debt burden of nearly ₹2 lakh crore comprising statutory dues. However, the latest relief significantly bolsters its ability to raise fresh funding and invest in network improvement to compete with larger rivals Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel.The government has made several interventions to keep India's third-largest telecom operator afloat. Under the 2021 telecom relief package, the government converted a portion of Vi's dues into equity, eventually raising its stake to 48.99%, making it the company's largest shareholder. In February 2023, nearly ₹16,000 crore of interest on deferred spectrum and AGR dues was converted into equity, giving the government about 33% stake at the time. This was followed by the conversion of an additional ₹36,950 crore of spectrum auction dues into equity in April 2025.

items.headline: Ryanair CEO dismisses Elon Musk's idea of buying airline as verbal feud escalates
items.body: Elon Musk Ryanair CEO dismissed Elon Musk's idea of buying the airline after a public spat O'Leary cited high Starlink Wi-Fi costs; Ryanair may explore alternatives. Ryanair used the feud for publicity, launching a Musk-themed seat sale. Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan The CEO of Ryanair on Wednesday dismissed Elon Musk's idea of buying the budget airline and shrugged off insults from the billionaire, in a war of words that erupted over installing Starlink systems on aircraft. The spat between one of the world's richest individuals and one of Europe's most outspoken corporate bosses has been escalating for days. O'Leary said last week that the airline had ruled out putting Musk's Starlink satellite Wi-Fi on Ryanair planes because the extra fuel drag from the system's antennas would be too costly. Responding to Musk's accusations that he was “misinformed,” O'Leary told an Irish radio station that "I would pay no attention whatsoever to Elon Musk , he's an idiot." Musk fired back on his social media platform X, calling O'Leary an “utter idiot” and an “imbecile.” He posted, “Should I buy Ryan Air and put someone whose actual name is Ryan in charge?” and polled his followers on the idea of buying the airline, with 76.5 per cent responding yes. O'Leary told reporters in Dublin, where Ryanair is based, that non-European citizens can't own a majority stake in a European airlines. Musk was born in South Africa and lives in the United States. “But if he wants to invest in Ryanair, we would think it's a very good investment. Certainly a significantly better investment than the financial returns he's earning on X,” O'Leary said. Related Stories Nikita Bier steps down as X product head after one year SpaceX's AI spending doubles to $15.8 billion in Q2 amid aggressive compute expansion SpaceX first earnings after IPO lands on August 4. Here's why all eyes are on it Musk purchased X in 2022 for $44 billion after clashing with top executives at the platform previously known as Twitter. O'Leary, who's known for trolling critics, thanked Musk for “additional publicity." The airline has taken advantage of the spat to launch a seat sale with promotional material featuring a caricature of Musk. He brushed off the billionaire's insults. “All I would say to Elon Musk is he would have to join the back of a very, very, very, very long queue of people” who have already insulted him, “including my four teenage children,” he said. O'Leary said Ryanair had been in discussions with Starlink for about 12 months on installing the system, “We like the Starlink system. It is a terrific system. It works very well,” he said, but adding it would cost the company about USD 250 million a year. That includes the cost of installing two antennas onto each aircraft fuselage, plus an extra 2 per cent of aerodynamic drag that would increase the fuel bill by USD200 million. Ryanair would have to charge for Starlink but O'Leary estimated that less than 5 per cent of passengers would want to spend a few extra euros for the service on its short-haul flights, which average about one hour and 15 minutes. The airline is still in talks with other telecommunications providers, including Amazon, which is launching its Starlink rival Kuiper, to provide onboard internet service, "but only in a way where it will lower our costs," O'Leary said. He also addressed a recent controversy around Musk's AI chatbot Grok, which is available through X and was being used to generate nonconsensual deepfake images. “Social media, X in particular is, a cesspit,” O'Leary said. “The most recent controversy with, you know, undressing children or undressing women is frankly offensive.” (AP) RD RD
items.snippet: The airline is still in talks with other telecommunications providers, including Amazon, which is launching its Starlink rival Kuiper, to provide onboard internet service, "but only in a way where it will lower our costs," O'Leary said.

items.headline: Malaysia replaced streetlights with roads that glow in the dark, but this futuristic idea, which promised
items.body: Amidst a dark, quiet section of the road within Hulu Langat, a futuristic idea once caught the attention of people and inspired imagination. At daytime the road appeared regular. After sunset, however, its roadway markings began to light up to guide motorists through the darkness with no need for street lights. The pilot program, which was launched through the Malaysian Public Works Department and reported by Radio Televisyen Malaysia, seemed to provide a straightforward yet powerful promise of safe roads and lower consumption of energy.In cities struggling with increasing cost of electricity and environmental worries, the notion of autonomously lit roads seemed ideal. If streets could be lit by themselves, the demand to install energy-inefficient streetlights would decrease. But, as Malaysia's history illustrates that even the most attractive technologies must be able to pass a more rooted test, which is price, durability, as well as scaling.The Pilot That Glowed With PromiseThe trials covered around 245 m of road with approximately 490 meters of luminescent designs that absorb light in the daytime and then emit an emitted light at night. The markings were applied in lieu of traditional reflective reflectors that are raised, also known by the name of cats' eyes. Officials, including the Works Minister Alexander Nanta Linggi, highlighted the way that glowing lines enhanced nighttime visibility, and may make drivers feel more safe and relaxed on roads that lack lighting infrastructure. In a country in which semi-urban and rural roads frequently do not have streetlights, this idea had a lot of appeal.The idea was inspired by earlier research similar to those of the Netherlands' Smart Highway project developed by Studio Roosegaarde, where glowing lines were reported to be in view for as long as eight hours following charging during daylight. The Malaysian trial was designed to test the effectiveness of this innovation with its specific circumstances, such as heavy rain and wear from traffic.130630713The Price of InnovationAlthough the results were visually pleasing however, the figures told an even more grim tale. The paint was photoluminescent with a price of RM749 each square meter as opposed to RM40 for traditional road markings. This made the glow option almost 19 times more costly without incorporating the cost of maintenance.Maintenance is a major problem. Roadmarkings can fade rapidly in the sun, rain, and the constant motion of vehicles. In hot climates such as Malaysia's, repainting sessions are frequent. That which looked stunning in an aircraft could turn out to be financially insufferable when rolled out across many kilometers.While Selangor officials announced initial plans to increase the number of LEDs to fifteen sites that would cover 15 km however, the financial cost was huge. However the government was investing a lot into LED street lighting by installing thousands of lighting fixtures and allocating large budgets to further expand.Parliament Pulls the PlugIn the latter half of 2024, the public's stance had changed dramatically. The deputy minister of works Ahmad Maslan informed lawmakers in Malaysia's Dewan Rakyat that the trial was not able to satisfy the expectations of experts. It was clear that it was cost prohibitive and the trial will likely cease.Instead, officials pointed to a simpler and more reliable solution--maintaining and repainting standard road markings to ensure visibility. This was not an outright refusal to innovate however, it was a recognition of the fact that infrastructure in public must be able to balance the need for performance and cost.The Energy Equation Behind the GlowThis experiment is also tied to an overall global problem. According to studies conducted by the U.S. Department of Energy the public area and street lighting could account for as much as 40 percent of the electricity consumed by municipal utilities worldwide. The reduction of this load is an important goal for cities seeking to decrease the carbon footprint and cost.The same institute states that LEDs is able to provide the required levels of illumination in less than half the power of traditional technology by using light to direct it more effectively. When it comes to practical applications, switching to LEDs and using smarter lighting controls could result in better and more cost-effective outcomes than the use of experimental coatings.Visibility Still Saves LivesIn the end, road safety relies on one crucial factor that is visibility. In the past, Federal Highway Administration has consistently stated that regularly maintained retroreflective pavement markings greatly improve nighttime driving conditions. The markings reflect the headlights towards drivers, allowing them to remain within the lane and respond to the road's circumstances.However, the organization observes that the markings can degrade rapidly and need regular care. This is a common occurrence in road conditions. In the dark of a storm blurred lines could make familiar roads seem unsafe and uncertain.Malaysia's experiment with glow-in the-dark confirms this point. Although the experiment caught attention however, the essentials of road safety - clear markings appropriate lighting, as well as regular maintenance are difficult to replace.What the Experiment Leaves BehindWhile the bright roads aren't likely to become an everyday thing in Malaysia however, the test did not fail in any way. It gave valuable insight into how drivers react to the new technologies, and also how these technologies work in real-world situations.Innovation usually begins with big concepts that don't instantly scale. This time, the bright lines were more than a single road. They showed the complicated balance between practicality and ambition in the public infrastructure.At present, the promise of night-time safety may consist less of glowing paint, and more in constant advancements to established methods. Sometimes, the most efficient methods aren't those with the latest technology however, they are the ones which quietly function every night.
items.snippet: Malaysia explored futuristic glow-in-the-dark road markings to enhance safety and reduce energy use.  The pilot project in Hulu Langat showed promise but proved too costly.  Officials found the innovative paint significantly more expensive than standard markings.  The government has now decided to focus on maintaining traditional road markings instead.  This approach prioritizes practicality and cost-effectiveness for public infrastructure.

items.headline: 7 winter office wear ideas that will make you look polished and effortlessly stylish
items.body: How to style a leather jacket: A well-cut leather jacket is no longer reserved for off-duty looks. In fact, it pairs beautifully with formal trousers, pencil skirts and crisp shirts (Image: Pexels) Choose breathable, insulating fabrics for sharp winter office looks Layer fleece leggings or thermal stockings to wear skirts and tunics in winter Enhance winter outfits with scarves, belts, and statement bags. Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Winter dressing for office does not have to mean bulky layers and boring colours. With smarter fabric choices, thoughtful layering and a little styling intent, your cold-weather wardrobe can feel just as sharp as your summer edit, only cosier. The secret to great winter office style is not about owning more layers, but choosing better ones. Prioritise fabrics that breathe yet insulate, silhouettes that allow movement, and accessories that do some of the styling work for you. 1. The luxe knit edit Soft knits are winter essentials, but the key is choosing elevated fabrics. Think merino wool sweaters, fine ribbed turtlenecks and cashmere-blend cardigans in neutral shades like oatmeal, mocha, charcoal and wine. Pair them with tailored trousers or midi skirts for a look that feels professional but never stiff. Add a structured tote and leather boots, and you have a reliable Monday-to-Friday uniform that feels both calm and confident. Also read | How to dress smart for office: Wear well-fitted clothes, good shoes to look sharp 2. Skirts, tunics and fleece leggings If you love skirts and long tunics, winter doesn’t mean giving them up. The trick lies in layering. Fleece-lined leggings or thermal stockings provide warmth without adding bulk, allowing you to continue wearing A-line skirts, shirt dresses and straight-cut tunics to work. Finish with knee-high boots and a long coat for a silhouette that feels sleek rather than overly layered. 3. The power sari with a shawl twist Winter workwear can be deeply stylish when you lean into Indian silhouettes. Lightweight wool saris, silk-cotton blends and handloom weaves pair beautifully with tailored blouses. Instead of hiding the drape under a coat, add a handcrafted shawl worn loosely over the shoulder. Pashmina, jamdani and fine wool shawls instantly add depth and texture while keeping you warm through meetings and commutes. Also read | Fashion tips: Avoid loud prints, colours and low necklines to look professional at work 4. Leather jackets meet formal staples A well-cut leather jacket is no longer reserved for off-duty looks. In fact, it pairs beautifully with formal trousers, pencil skirts and crisp shirts. A black or tan leather jacket over a monochrome outfit instantly sharpens your presence without trying too hard. This works especially well for creative workplaces, client meetings and after-work plans when you want your outfit to transition seamlessly. 5. Soft layers with a boho spirit If your personal style leans more relaxed, winter is the perfect season to embrace colour and texture. Think layered cotton dresses with sleeveless jackets, earthy-toned stoles, block-printed scarves and handcrafted jewellery. Choose warm fabrics like brushed cotton, handloom wool blends and quilted overlays. The result is a look that feels expressive yet thoughtful, ideal for professionals who like their wardrobe to reflect personality. 6. K-Drama inspired tailoring Korean fashion has had a strong influence on global workwear, and winter styling borrows heavily from its clean, cosy aesthetic. Oversized blazers, straight trousers, soft sweaters layered under structured coats, and muted colour palettes like greys, creams and dusty pastels define this look. Add minimal sneakers or ankle boots, and you have a contemporary work outfit that feels relaxed but still sharply put together. 7. Formal suits, elevated with accessories A classic winter suit can go from predictable to stylish with the right accessories. Think silk scarves tucked into blazers, statement belts over longline jackets, bold watches and structured handbags. Even something as simple as switching from basic studs to sculptural earrings can transform a neutral suit. Winter fabrics like tweed, wool blends and heavier crepes also add depth without compromising on professionalism.
items.snippet: Winter office wear ideas: From sari styling to K-drama inspired tailoring, here are seven workwear ideas that balance comfort, warmth and fashion-forward appeal.

items.headline: Give your bathroom a more intimate and lived-in vibe with these easy expert decor ideas
items.body: Bathroom decor tips: Wet-room layouts, built-in seating, and immersive shower zones are gaining popularity, encouraging longer, more mindful water rituals (Images: Grohe) Bathrooms are now designed as personal sanctuaries with emotional intent Warm colors, natural materials, and modular concepts create restorative spaces Tech in bathrooms is discreet, enhancing comfort without disrupting calm Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Across urban homes, bathrooms are evolving as deeply personal space that reflects lifestyle, mood, and wellbeing. Homeowners are shaping them with the same care given to living rooms and bedrooms, creating spaces that feel restorative, expressive, and emotionally grounding. Morning routines, evening wind-down rituals, and moments of solitude are influencing design decisions. This shift is driving a move away from standardised layouts toward more thoughtful, customised spaces that feel intimate and lived-in. Designers are responding with warmer, earth-inspired colour palettes and authentic materials such as stone, wood textures, and tactile finishes. These elements introduce softness and familiarity, moving bathrooms away from the cold, clinical look that once dominated. Design excellence with emotional intent Alongside aesthetics, the structure of bathroom design is becoming more intentional. Layouts are now cleaner, more restrained, and guided by a clear purpose. Priya Rustogi, Leader (MD), India, LIXIL IMEA, tells Moneycontrol , “This evolution is also about purpose. Every material choice, lighting decision, and spatial transition is increasingly linked to how the space makes people feel. Bathrooms are being designed as private sanctuaries, with thoughtful entry sequences, ambient lighting, and acoustic comfort that help users transition from the pace of the city into a moment of pause.” Also read | Give your bathroom a quick makeover with these 7 impressive décor ideas Lighting is softer and layered, acoustics are considered more carefully, and transitions from other parts of the home are designed to feel intentional rather than abrupt. Modular concepts Another defining trend is flexibility. Modular shower concepts are now seen as essential rather than indulgent. Homeowners want the freedom to customise their experience, combining overhead showers, side sprays, and finishes that feel personal. Says Rustogi, “These elements encourage the bathroom to be used as a place for restoration rather than efficiency alone. Variable spray patterns and flow intensities allow users to adapt water delivery to different moments of the day, supporting both energising routines and quieter, restorative pauses.” Also read | 5 luxurious bathroom design ideas you can recreate in any space Wet-room layouts , built-in seating, and immersive shower zones are gaining popularity, encouraging longer, more mindful water rituals. The bathroom becomes less about rushing through a routine and more about slowing down, even if only for a few minutes each day. Tech-enabled yet discreet As smart homes become mainstream, technology in bathrooms is being approached with more sensitivity. Unlike living spaces where screens and devices are welcome, bathrooms are still seen as zones of calm. Homeowners are increasingly wary of overt tech that disrupts the atmosphere. The most successful innovations are those that work quietly in the background. Rustogi explains, “Digital thermostatic controls play a critical role in enabling this shift. By delivering precise temperature and flow control through intuitive interfaces, they remove complexity while enhancing comfort and safety. Advanced systems allow users to personalise their experience with accuracy and consistency, without disrupting the visual calm of the space.” At a broader level, this reflects a move toward designing complete water behaviour systems rather than isolated fixtures. Embedded technology is now designed to support architectural intent rather than compete with it. These systems are also adaptable, evolving with household needs and life stages without requiring major structural changes.
items.snippet: Modern bathroom decor ideas: The growing popularity of sensory showers and thoughtfully designed bathrooms signals a deeper cultural shift. People are investing in spaces that support mental clarity, emotional comfort, and everyday wellbeing.

items.headline: Warren Buffett's son reveals surprising moment when he realised his father was billionaire: 'I had no idea'
items.body: Warren Buffett with his son Peter Buffett. (Image credit: Representative photo/Yahoo) Peter Buffett learned of his father's wealth only in his 20s Warren Buffett raised his children humbly despite immense fortune Peter Buffett is a musician, author, and co-chair of the NoVo Foundation Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Warren Buffett, former CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, topped the list of the world’s richest people in 2008 with $62 billion, surpassing Bill Gates net worth. Surprisingly, his youngest son, Peter Buffett, remained largely unaware of how wealthy and influential his father was for years. Speaking to Fortune, Peter Buffett only realised how powerful his father was in his 20s, during a casual conversation with his mother, following noticing his father's name on Forbes’ list of the richest Americans. “I’m not kidding. It was when I was in my 20s that my mom and I talked at some point, because there he was, on this list,” Peter told Forbes in 2013. “And we laughed about it, because we said, ‘Well, isn’t it funny? You know, we know who we are, but everybody’s treating us differently now. "Our friends were as surprised as I was," he added. At the Forbes' Second Annual Summit on Philanthropy in 2013, Warren Buffett sat next to his son, discussing how humbly his children were raised despite immense wealth. "Our kids had a very normal growing-up. They did not ride in private planes. They went to school on the bus," Buffett said. "I just lived the life I wanted to live, and my wife lived the life she wanted to live. There wasn't anything that we wanted that we didn't have, but we didn't crave a lot of possessions," he told Forbes. Related Stories Warren Buffett credits success to being a 'white male' in US: Had confidence that I would be rich What is the point of Berkshire Hathaway? SpaceX rally adds $164 billion to Musk's fortune, more than Buffett's net worth About Peter Buffett Peter Buffett, now 67, is the youngest child of Warren Buffett and Susan Buffett. Peter has established himself as a musician, composer, author and philanthropist. His achievements include a regional Emmy Award, New York Times best-selling author, and serving as co-chair of the NoVo Foundation. Warren Buffett’s net worth Once the richest in the world, Warren Buffett had a net worth of $62 billion. Although he is no longer the world’s richest man, he remains one of the top 10 wealthiest individuals globally, with a current net worth of approximately $145 billion.
items.snippet: Warren Buffett’s youngest son, Peter, revealed that his father’s billionaire status only became real to him in his 20s, after seeing him featured on Forbes’ list.

items.headline: Davos 2026: “The idea that AI equals Nvidia has been crossed, and its dominance is being challenged,” says Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman
items.body: Andrew Feldman Cerebras Nvidia's dominance in AI chips is being challenged, says Cerebras CEO Feldman Google trained Gemini AI without Nvidia hardware, marking a major industry shift. Cerebras positions its Wafer Scale Engine as a strong competitor to Nvidia Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan The long-held belief that artificial intelligence is synonymous with Nvidia’s GPUs is now being challenged, said Andrew Feldman, co-founder and CEO of AI chipmaker Cerebras, in an interview with Moneycontrol’s Chandra R Srikanth on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum 2026 in Davos. “I think we’ve already seen Nvidia’s dominance being challenged. The GPU is not the only machine that can be used in AI. The mental moat for those who thought that AI equalled Nvidia has been crossed,” Feldman said. He also cited Nvidia’s reported $20 billion acquisition of Groq as proof of this transition. “Nvidia admitted they didn’t have a solution and spent $20 billion to buy the number two player. That shows there are things GPUs don’t do well,” he said. In December of 2025, Nvidia Corp. agreed to a licensing deal with artificial intelligence startup Groq, furthering its investments in companies connected to the AI boom and gaining the right to add a new type of technology to its products. Related Stories Cerebras shares skyrocket in debut as AI mania grips markets Børge Brende quits as World Economic Forum CEO over Epstein links: What were the allegations? WEF chief Borge Brende steps down following review of Epstein ties, Alois Zwinggi to take over The world’s largest publicly traded company has paid for the right to use Groq’s technology and will integrate its chip design into future products. Some of the startup’s executives are leaving to join Nvidia to help with that effort, the companies said. Groq will continue as an independent company with a new chief executive, it said Wednesday in a post on its website. Feldman pointed to Google training its Gemini model on TPUs without using Nvidia hardware as a major shift in the industry. “What we saw was the training of a foundation model entirely without Nvidia. That was a big moment,” he said. Feldman said the market is now rapidly moving toward fast inference, the stage where AI is deployed in real-world applications. “Inference is where AI meets the real economy. That’s where coding, agentic work and deep research happen,” he said. Founded in 2016, Cerebras Systems specialises in AI computing with its flagship product, the Wafer Scale Engine (WSE), the world’s largest AI accelerator. The company is positioning itself as a strong competitor to industry giants like NVIDIA by providing cutting-edge AI hardware solutions for enterprises and research institutions. Asked whether Cerebras itself had received acquisition interest, Feldman replied, “We don’t kiss and tell. We’re gentlemen.” On concerns of an AI bubble, Feldman dismissed the idea. “This isn’t a bubble. This is how a new technology diffuses through an entire economy...People want AI to be faster. They don’t want to wait. Faster inference is what users care about most today,” he added.
items.snippet: Andrew Feldman says Nvidia’s dominance is being challenged as fast inference reshapes the AI chip market.

items.body: With campaigning for the West Bengal Assembly elections concluding on April 27, exit polls for West Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry will be declared on April 29 after 6:30 pm. Voting for Phase 2 of the West Bengal Assembly elections is scheduled for April 29, with the silence period in force until 6:00 pm the same day. During this time, all media platforms are prohibited from publishing or broadcasting election-related content. Restrictions on media and opinion pollsThe Election Commission has directed television, radio channels and cable networks to ensure that content broadcast during the silence period does not include material that could influence voters or affect the outcome of the election. This includes any form of opinion polls or views that may promote or prejudice the prospects of candidates or parties.Also Read: West Bengal elections 2026: As Kolkata votes tomorrow, check IMD's weather forecast on day of TMC vs BJP high-stakes clashExit poll ban timeline and penaltiesMedia organisations have been informed that conducting and publishing exit polls is prohibited from 7:00 am on April 9 until 6:30 pm on April 29. The elections have seen the Bharatiya Janata Party attempting to unseat the Mamata Banerjee led government in West Bengal and expand its presence in Tamil Nadu, while the Trinamool Congress is seeking a fourth consecutive term.The second phase of polling in West Bengal will cover the remaining 142 of the total 294 seats on April 29.
