This includes adjusted gross revenue liabilities. The dues will be frozen as of December 2025 and repaid over 15 years. This offers crucial cash flow relief to the company.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea confirms AGR relief, says Rs 124 crore to be paid annually over next 6 years
items.body: Vodafone Idea on Friday confirmed that its adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues for the period from FY 2006–07 to FY 2018–19 will remain frozen from December 31, 2025.As per the plan outlined by the telecom company, it will be required to pay Rs 124 crore annually over the next six years, from March 2026 to March 2031. After this period, the operator will pay Rs 100 crore annually over four years, from March 2032 to March 2035. The remaining AGR dues will be paid in equal annual instalments over six years, from March 2036 to March 2041.Shares in the telecom operator gained 7.8% to their intraday high of Rs 12.40 on the BSE in early trade on Friday. Additionally, the cash-strapped telecom operator said that a committee is to be constituted by DoT to reassess the AGR dues, whose decision shall be final.AGR dues refer to payments owed by telecom companies to the government based on their Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR). It is the revenue on which telecom operators must pay license fees and spectrum usage charges. It is defined to include all revenues, even non-telecom income (like interest, rent, asset sales). Vodafone Idea has been battling a prolonged financial crisis, driven by intense price competition, massive AGR liabilities, and high debt that arose from a change in the definition of AGR. The company has been facing a number of struggles like persistent losses, a shrinking subscriber base, and limited ability to invest in network expansion, even as rivals accelerated 4G and 5G rollouts.
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea's adjusted gross revenue dues from FY 2006-07 to FY 2018-19 will be frozen from December 31, 2025. The company will pay a maximum of Rs. 124 crore annually until March 2031, followed by Rs. 100 crore annually until March 2035. Remaining dues will be paid in equal installments from March 2036 to March 2041.

items.headline: Motilal Oswal sees 8% YoY growth in Nifty Q3 earnings; SBI, Eternal among 5 top ideas
items.body: The October-December quarter earnings are expected to register their highest growth in eight quarters on an improved earnings environment, with the Nifty likely delivering an 8% year-on-year growth, Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said in a note. Meanwhile, earnings by companies under MOFSL’s coverage universe may report a 25% year-on-year growth.Excluding financials, earnings for the MOFSL universe and the Nifty 50 are expected to grow 19% and 9% YoY, respectively. Further, barring metals and oil & gas (O&G), earnings are projected to rise 14% YoY for the MOFSL universe and 11% YoY for the Nifty 50, highlighting broad-based growth across several sectors.The overall earnings momentum in Q3FY26 is expected to be driven by oil & gas, where profits are estimated to jump 25% YoY, and financials, led by NBFC lending companies with a 26% growth.Automobiles are projected to deliver a 25% YoY increase in earnings, while metals are seen growing 15%. Telecom profits are expected to jump 2.6 times over a low base in Q3FY25, while technology sector earnings are likely to rise 8%.Other key contributors include real estate, where earnings are projected to surge 64% YoY, capital goods at 24%, cement at 66%, and NBFC non-lending firms at 31%. Together, these sectors are expected to account for nearly 77% of the incremental YoY earnings accretion during the quarter.In contrast, earnings contribution from banks is expected to remain modest, with private banks seen growing profits by 4% YoY and public sector banks by 3%. Infrastructure and media sectors are likely to drag overall earnings, with profits estimated to decline 3% and 7% YoY, respectively.FY26 outlookLooking ahead, MOFSL expects FY26 earnings for Nifty companies to grow 8% YoY, and excluding financials, FY26 earnings are expected to rise 7% YoY. Further, barring metals and O&G, FY26 earnings growth is estimated at 8% YoY for the Nifty 50.As for the broader MOFSL universe, profit is projected to record a 14% YoY increase in the full financial year. Excluding financials, FY26 earnings are expected to rise 17% YoY, the note said. Excluding metals and O&G, a 12% YoY growth is expected for the broader universe.However, MOFSL has trimmed its FY26 and FY27 Nifty EPS estimates by 2.2% and 1.1%, respectively, and now expects it to grow 9% YoY in FY26 to Rs 1,084, followed by a 15% growth in FY27 to Rs 1,267.The downward revision has largely been driven by weaker expectations from the metals, oil & gas, financials and consumer sectors, the note said.MOFSL’s top 5 Nifty 50 ideasThe brokerage’s top Nifty ideas include PSU lender State Bank of India (SBI), Titan Company, Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M), Infosys and Eternal.Top 5 non-Nifty ideasDixon Technologies, Indian Hotels, Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww), TVS Motors and Radico Khaitan.Sectoral ratingsMOFSL remains ‘Overweight’ on autos, diversified financials, industrials and EMS, consumer discretionary and technology. It remains ‘Underweight’ on oil & gas, metals and consumer staples.2026 market outlookThe brokerage noted multiple levers to propel Indian equity markets in 2026. “In CY25, India had to endure a constant flow of disproportionate and punitive US trade measures, which were instrumental in catalysing a USD 19 billion in FII outflows. However, the government and the RBI have been active in mitigating external headwinds and have adopted several stimulative fiscal, monetary and reform measures to unshackle domestic growth impulses,” the note said.In its opinion, these measures should now start to manifest in full force in 2026, and MOFSL sees limited domestic risk factors thwarting this.Despite these challenges, the Nifty eked out early double-digit gains in CY25, rising 11%, with the broader Nifty 500 growing 7%, though it underperformed global indices materially. The MSCI EM index jumped 31% while MSCI AXJ rallied 30% in the same period.However, geopolitics and global trade continue to be a strong caveat and could cast a shadow of chronic risk aversion for equity markets, the note warned. Also Read | Quant Small Cap Fund adds Adani Green Energy and 3 other stocks, exits LIC in December(Disclaimer: The recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times.)

items.headline: Quote of the day by comic creator legend Stan Lee: 'If you have an idea that you think is good, don’t let
items.body: If you have an idea that you genuinely think is good, don’t let some idiot talk you out of it. Now, that doesn't mean that every wild notion you come up with is going to be genius, but if there is something that you feel is good, something you want to do, something that means something to you, try to do it, because I think you can only do your best work if you're doing what you want to do. – Stan LeeIn a world full of critics, doubters, and unsolicited advice, the legendary comic book creator Stan Lee reminds us that great ideas start with belief in yourself. His words said during his Keynote Address at UCLA Extension Certificate Graduation Ceremony in 2017 are a gentle nudge to trust your instincts and pursue what you love, no matter what anyone says.126371295 Don’t Let Anyone Steal Your SparkLee’s quote might sound playful, but it carries a serious message about courage and conviction. He encouraged creators and dreamers to stand by their ideas, even when others dismiss them. The story of Spider-Man illustrates this perfectly. When Lee pitched the concept to his publisher, it was rejected as the “worst idea” ever. Teenagers were not considered heroes, and spiders were widely feared. Lee ignored the criticism, and Spider-Man debuted in Amazing Fantasy #15, quickly becoming a cultural phenomenon.He often added that doing your best work depends on doing what you genuinely believe is right, in the way you want to do it. Passion and personal conviction are the fuel of excellence.Why These Words Still Matter TodayIn today’s fast-paced world of instant opinions and social media commentary, it’s easy to doubt yourself. Lee’s advice is a reminder that innovation rarely comes from following the crowd.Whether you’re launching a startup, writing a novel, designing art, or pursuing a personal passion, external doubt should never define your limits. Great ideas often face initial resistance, but persistence and confidence turn those ideas into impact. Stan Lee’s words encourage us to trust our intuition and embrace the value of creative risk.126320317 The Man Behind the MagicStanley Martin Lieber, better known as Stan Lee, was born in 1922 and joined Timely Comics at age 17. Over decades, he co-created legendary characters including Spider-Man, Iron Man, the X-Men, Thor, and the Fantastic Four, giving superheroes human flaws and relatable struggles.Lee revolutionized storytelling with the “Marvel Method,” blending plot outlines with artist-driven creativity. He used comics to address social issues, pushing boundaries and expanding Marvel into a global multimedia empire. Even after retiring, he remained a beloved public figure, with memorable cameos in Marvel films, inspiring new generations of creators.Honors followed his influence: Lee was inducted into the Will Eisner Award Hall of Fame and the Jack Kirby Hall of Fame, and in 2008 he received the National Medal of Arts. His life proves that following your ideas with conviction can leave a legacy that transcends time, pages, and screens.Stan Lee’s advice is timeless: believe in your ideas, follow your instincts, and do your best work. Success does not come from approval but from courage, creativity, and persistence. Every breakthrough starts with trusting yourself, even when the world doubts you.126283457
items.snippet: Stan Lees timeless advice, delivered at a 2017 UCLA ceremony, offers a powerful reminder about believing in ones ideas despite criticism. Using Spider-Mans unlikely origin as proof, the comic legend showed how conviction and passion fuel meaningful work. In an era shaped by instant opinions and constant doubt, Lees words resonate strongly with creators, entrepreneurs, and dreamers alike. His life and legacy underline a simple truth: innovation demands courage, creative risk, and trust in ones instincts, even when the world is skeptical.

items.headline: Kya expansionist idea, Ramboji! What Trumpâs Maduro capture reveals to the world & India
items.body: Governments across the world are trying to examine whether the capture of Nicolas Maduro by US forces has thrown up lessons for them. For India, the key takeaway is collapse of China's air defence system in Venezuela during Saturday's assault. This comes 7 months after Indian forces destroyed several Pakistani airbases, exposing the vulnerabilities of China-made radars.Several countries are also worried about the ability of US intelligence agencies and their cyber support teams to infiltrate security apparatuses. This was earlier seen during US strikes of Iran's nuclear facilities in June 2025. Despite some quarters being impressed by the US operation in Venezuela, what Trump has done is open Pandora's box, which could destabilise regions and threaten world peace.The US had given sufficient indication that it would take 'action' against Maduro. But none of Venezuela's allies - China, Russia and Iran - provided the Venezuelan president with any actionable intelligence or coordinated military support.The image of China, which positions itself as an alternative power centre that runs counter to a unipolar, US-centric world that has eschewed international order, has been tarnished. Beijing may be forced to re-examine its influence-building strategy, which involves participating in joint military exercises and investing billions in infrastructure projects. Some experts have questioned the wisdom of investing $65 bn in a BRI programme in Pakistan.The latest US assault may lead to American companies controlling the world's biggest oil reserve, provided they gain effective control over Venezuela. But there are doubts because Delcy Rodriguez, of the ruling United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV) led by Maduro, remains acting president, whom Trump is threatening with additional strikes if she does not toe the US line.It's being argued that Washington will have no moral right to intervene if China invades Taiwan, Israel tries to capture Gaza, Russia takes control of more regions in Ukraine, or India decides to 'take action' in POK. But Trump is less keen on occupying the moral high ground than he is on getting his hands on resources, including oil, in other countries.Beijing has two choices. Xi Jinping can attack Taiwan before Taipei obtains more sophisticated weapons systems from Washington and replace the elected leaders with his nominees. Or he can concentrate on China's economic growth and enhance China's ability to equal, or even overtake, the US before invading Taiwan. In the process, Xi could choose to enhance China's current attempts to come across as the more stable global power respecting an international rules-based order. Engaging Taiwan militarily at this time could invite US intervention, which would distract China from its economic growth plan, and make Xi's China just another 'Trump's US'.The capture of Maduro may, indeed, trigger a chain reaction among other regimes with the capability to forgo the idea of nation-state sovereignty. It could certainly prompt countries to intensify their programmes of militarisation and use of military force as instruments of economic and foreign policy. So, beyond the 'GI Joe' shock and awe in Venezuela, Trump has certainly made countries less inhibited about an expansionist strategy, and the world a less secure place.The writer is former ToI correspondent in Beijing
items.snippet: The US capture of Nicolas Maduro offers lessons for nations. China's air defense systems faced exposure. US intelligence capabilities are a concern. This event could destabilize regions and threaten world peace. China may rethink its influence strategy. Countries might become less inhibited about expansionist policies. The world faces increased insecurity.

items.headline: Archana Puran Singh reveals how husband Parmeet Sethi reacted when son Aaryamann was born: ‘He had no idea
items.body: Archana Puran Singh is currently soaking in a family vacation in London, blending leisure with heartfelt celebrations. In her recent vlog update, the popular actor and judge from The Great Indian Kapil Show offered viewers a behind-the-scenes look at an emotional and thoughtfully planned surprise marking her elder son Aaryamann’s 30th birthday. The video captured the meticulous preparations that went into making the milestone memorable, led largely by Aaryamann’s fiancée, actor Yogita Bihani.Yogita curated an engaging treasure hunt that ultimately led Aaryamann to a lavish and deeply personal present — a premium guitar valued at approximately Rs 2.12 lakh. Given Aaryamann’s identity as a musician and digital creator, the gift held special meaning, symbolising both his artistic journey and the affection of his partner. The vlog documented the excitement, secrecy, and teamwork involved in pulling off the surprise, with Archana playing an enthusiastic role in the planning.Amid the preparations, the video also showcased light-hearted exchanges between Archana and her husband, actor Parmeet Sethi. Their playful back-and-forth added warmth and humour, particularly when Archana jokingly remarked that Parmeet had little understanding of fatherhood three decades ago. The banter unfolded naturally, reflecting the couple’s easy camaraderie and long-standing bond.The moment turned reflective when Archana revisited the day Aaryamann was born. She shared a poignant thought about motherhood, expressing how a child’s birthday is often celebrated without acknowledging the transformation a woman undergoes on that day. For her, that date was not just about welcoming her son into the world but also about her own rebirth as a mother, marking a profound personal milestone.Parmeet responded in jest, insisting that fathers also play an equal role in bringing up a child and teasingly accused society of overlooking paternal contributions. His humorous protest led to more laughter, especially as Archana pointed out how unconvincing his argument sounded even to himself. When Yogita attempted to ask Parmeet about his emotions on becoming a father, Archana quickly interjected, reiterating that he had been largely unaware of what fatherhood truly entailed at the time. He had no idea what being a father meant at the time, she joked. Archana and Parmeet tied the knot on June 30, 1992, after living together for four years. Together, they are parents to two sons, Aaryamann and Ayushmaan, and continue to share moments of affection, humour, and reflection as a family.
items.snippet: Archana Puran Singh celebrated her elder son Aaryamann's 30th birthday in London with a surprise treasure hunt planned by his fiancée, Yogita Bihani. The event featured a thoughtful gift of a premium guitar and light-hearted family banter, including Archana's reflections on motherhood.

items.headline: Internet players, non-telcos demand AGR relief after Voda Idea's big breather
items.body: New Delhi: Relief granted to Vodafone Idea on its adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues has triggered demand for similar government support from hundreds of standalone internet service providers (ISPs) and other non-telcos struggling under hefty AGR liabilities.These firms face AGR dues running into thousands of crores following a 2019 Supreme Court ruling, which prompted the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to raise demands against several companies beyond telcos, including ISPs, VSAT operators and public sector entities. Many of the smaller firms are struggling financially due to intense competition, not only from contemporaries but also from big telecom firms, said Rajesh Chharia, president of Internet Service Providers Association of India (ISPAI). The ISPs, too, are saddled with thousands of crores of AGR dues and a similar relief or waiver should also be given to these firms, he told ET.The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a relief package that gives Vodafone Idea (Vi) a 10-year breather to pay more than 95% of its AGR dues. The dues till FY17 have also been frozen at ₹87,695 crore as on December 31, 2025, and a committee would be formed to reassess the dues. The government giving relief to Vi gives hope to thousands of standalone ISPs, who are eagerly waiting for implementing DCC (Digital Communications Commission)-approved policy of making fixed line broadband services free from 8% licence fees on revenue for 10 years, Chharia said.ISPAI represents over 100 ISPs including Sify, Tikona, Tata Communications, Powergrid, Tata Sky, Connect Broadband, Netmagic and Excitel.DoT officials, however, stressed that other companies seeking similar relief must get the top court's nod for the same. The package to Vi has been given following the top court order, which specifically asked that the order applies to the company only, one of the officials told ET on condition of anonymity.Industry players argue that the scale of AGR liabilities across telecom and non-telecom sectors raises larger policy questions.Bharti Airtel, which is scheduled to pay over Rs 42,000 crore in AGR dues starting next fiscal, has made it clear that it will approach DoT, seeking reassessment.In November 2024, Bharti Airtel’s Executive Vice Chairman Gopal Vittal said the company would engage with the government on the AGR matter after the Supreme Court allowed a comprehensive reassessment and reconciliation of liabilities, including interest and penalties, on a plea by Vi.The company, however, has yet to apply and formally seek a relief on the lines of Vi.Legal RecourseA query sent to Airtel on the issue remained unanswered at the time of going to press.Non-telecom firms are saddled with over ₹82,000 crore of AGR dues.Initial demands from DoT totalled more than ₹4 lakh crore for non-telcos.Later, the department withdrew nearly 96% of demand for AGR dues for some state-run firms such as ONGC, PowerGrid and GAIL India. This prompted some firms to seek legal recourse for similar treatment.So far, Vi is the only private company that has got support from the government. The latest relief package allows the telco another shot at survival as it would be able to now raise funds to remain competitive.Chharia noted ISPs form the backbone of the country’s broadband infrastructure, particularly in rural India.
items.snippet: AGR relief: These firms face AGR dues running into thousands of crores following a 2019 Supreme Court ruling, which prompted the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to raise demands against several companies beyond telcos, including ISPs, VSAT operators and public sector entities.

items.headline: 6 investment ideas that can win 2026 for you: AI adoption, FIIs, gold among 6 wealth creation themes picked by
items.body: AI adoption, trade tariff resolution and central bank policies are among 6 key themes that could drive wealth creation in 2026, according to the 2026 Outlook by ASK Private Wealth, the wealth management arm of the Blackstone-backed ASK Asset & Wealth Management Group. The wealth management company unveiled these six themes in its report titled “2026: Six Themes and One Worry Not.” Here are the six investable themes that can help create wealth in 2026 as per the ASK Private Wealth report, and a look at what makes these themes unique. AI adoptionTrade tariff resolutionCentral banks’ policiesSectoral rotationFII interestMainstreaming of alternativesLet's discuss what the wealth management company says in its outlook for the year ahead.1. What makes AI strong bet in 2026The outlook report highlights artificial intelligence (AI) as the first theme for creating money-making opportunities. It mentions that the ongoing AI boom is driven by earnings instead of speculation, which helps keep valuations in check.The report underlines key areas that position AI as a smart investment choice for 2026-Mega-cap tech earnings continue to outpace the rest of the market.Spending on AI is surging among China’s internet platforms.The percentage of S&P firms mentioning artificial intelligence (AI) during 3Q25 has risen to 62%.The report claims that the current AI boom is backed by growth, while the tech boom in 1998-2000 was led by valuation. 2. Resolution of India-US trade tariff issueThe 2026 outlook claims that a tariff resolution is likely between India and the US, which will benefit various sectors in India. In 2025, US tariffs on Indian exports affected numerous industries in India such as textiles, gems, jewellery, marine and chemicals. The 2026 outlook indicates that there are more factors in favour of a tariff deal between India and the US than there are against it.As per the report, despite tariff-related uncertainties, India has handled the situation well, with the overall trade balance remaining steady and the currency tracking within historical norms. The report says that some of the areas that will benefit from India-US tariff resolution are trade and tariffs, visa and immigration, geopolitics, economic and market, social and cultural and emerging opportunities. 3. Central bank rate cuts have enough space for equity putThe 2026 outlook says that both the Indian and US central banks have room to cut rates, but action may be delayed to maintain financial stability—acting as a support for equities.The report says that strong policy buffers with real interest rates elevated across major economies are providing central banks with room to stabilise markets if volatility increases. Currently, real policy rates are ruling at or close to their highest level in 10 years. In India, real policy rates are the highest in a decade, while in the US, they are ruling significantly above average. The report highlights these factors as potential catalysts for equity growth in 2026.4. Sectoral rotation creating investment opportunitiesThe report indicates that traditional sectoral winners are losing their staying power, which might impact performance, but it’s also opening up some unique opportunities. The report says that certain factors contributing to sectoral rotation being a strong bet include the correlation between declining sector performance and the Nifty’s strong performance across sectors. 5. FIIs interest increases in Indian banks and real estateThe 2026 outlook report claims that foreign institutional investors' interest in Indian banks and real estate is rising, indicating that FIIs are likely to return to the Indian market."Foreign investors are likely to return, as demonstrated by their strategic interest in the banking and real estate sector, as valuations align with earnings," as per the report.Citing recent deals where FIIs increased their stake in Indian banks and real estate companies, the report says that a continued momentum in real estate is expected in 2025–2026 amid favourable economic fundamentals and global portfolio shifts. 6. Mainstream alternatives gaining prominenceThe report says that alternatives like gold, hybrids, and private markets will gain prominence in 2026. In private markets, selection will be key to returns, the report claims.As per the outlook, gold presents a strong investment case since central banks are purchasing it, the yellow metal's demand for ETF remains strong, the demand-supply balance is in its favour, and interest rates are low. The report says that strong growth and stellar performance of hybrid investments such as Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) make them a strong investment bet. About the private market, the report says that the market presents a plethora of opportunities, and growth depends on the selection of stocks.
items.snippet: ASK Private Wealth's 2026 Outlook identifies six key themes for wealth creation, including AI adoption, trade tariff resolution, and central bank policies. The report highlights AI's earnings-driven growth, potential India-US tariff deal benefits, and room for central bank rate cuts.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea seen getting decade-long relief; AGR dues of ₹87,000 crore may halve after review with payme
items.body: New Delhi: Vodafone Idea (Vi) has technically got a 10-year breather to pay more than 95% of its adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues, officials said, referring to the pivotal relief package that would allow the struggling telco to recover financially. Vi stock, which had slumped on Wednesday, surged Thursday after some clarity emerged on potential benefit to the company.Vodafone Idea's shares opened higher on BSE Sensex on Friday and were up nearly 2.5% in initial trade.Officials told ET the government has frozen Vi's AGR dues at ₹87,695 crore as on December 31. A committee will be formed within three to four months to reassess dues, they said. After the reassessment, ₹87,695 crore will go down substantially and whatever the new amount comes, it has to be paid by FY36 to FY41, said an official on the condition of anonymity, as the details are not public yet.Also Read: Vodafone Idea receives Rs 638 crore GST penalty order; co says it will take legal actionWhen the company had approached the Supreme Court earlier, it wanted time until FY41 to pay the AGR dues. The government has basically granted the company the necessary time to recover, said another official. 126296420 Until FY36, Vi will be paying around ₹114 crore annually for six years, starting the current fiscal until FY31 and ₹100 crore annually for another four years until FY35, said one of the officials cited above. As the company is technically paying some amount every year, there is no moratorium in the repayment schedule as such.While there is a clean five-year moratorium for the frozen dues, which will be reassessed, the company has to pay AGR dues for FY18 and FY19. The amount is ₹700-800 crore and has to be paid by FY31 as ₹114 crore in annual instalments, said a second official.Shares of the telco closed at ₹11.62 apiece, up about 8% on the BSE on Thursday. The stock price hit a lower circuit a day earlier, when reports emerged about the relief package, which ruled out any waiver of dues. However, after clarity today (Thursday) around the potential of the package, the stock has bounced back, said an analyst.The Supreme Court order on AGR dues came in October 2019 and that order had accounted for dues until FY17.Another 5-yr Moratorium Based on the order, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) calculated dues for FY18 and FY19 too, and raised the demand for payment by telecom firms, including Vi and Bharti Airtel.In September 2021, the government granted a four-year moratorium on AGR dues until FY19 to telcos, which included dues of the apex court order. The moratorium ends with this fiscal.Now, Vi has got another five-year moratorium for AGR dues until FY17, and it has to pay for FY18 and FY19 in the manner outlined above.But even from FY32, when repayment of the majority of AGR dues commences, Vofadone Idea won't be paying equal instalments until FY36, as it has to pay its spectrum dues. The company has to pay Rs 100 crore from FY32 to FY36, and the remaining AGR dues have to be paid between FY36 and FY41, said the second official.The first official cited said by FY36, the majority of Vi's spectrum auction dues would have been paid, and the company will be in a much better financial situation. Overall, the telco has to pay spectrum dues till FY44.The government would have been the biggest loser if Vofadone Idea were to go bust, as it has the majority 49% stake in the telco. Aditya Birla Group and the UK's Vodafone Group Plc hold 9.50% and 16.07%, respectively.
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea has secured a 10-year extension on its Adjusted Gross Revenue payments, a move that has been confirmed by officials who have frozen the owed amount. Anticipated adjustments are expected to bring down the total significantly, providing much-needed financial respite to the company.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea shares in focus on receiving Rs 638 crore GST order
items.body: Shares of telecom operator Vodafone Idea are expected to remain in the spotlight on Friday, January 2, after the telecom company disclosed that it had received a significant tax-related order from the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) authorities. The order, dated December 31, 2025, confirms a demand of Rs 637.9 crore, including penalty and interest.The order was issued by the Office of the Additional Commissioner, CGST, Ahmedabad South, and pertains to allegations of short payment of tax and excess availment of input tax credit by the company.The total demand raised amounts to Rs 6,37,90,68,254, and includes applicable interest and penalties.Sensex, Nifty today: Catch all the LIVE stock market action here Vodafone Idea, in a regulatory filing, clarified that it does not agree with the contents of the order and intends to pursue appropriate legal action.“Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Clause 20 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III of SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, we submit the details of orders received by the Company under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. The Company disagrees with the Order and will take appropriate legal action(s) against the same,” the company said in an exchange filing.While the company did not provide a detailed breakdown of the financial implications, it confirmed that the maximum impact would be equivalent to the total amount of tax, penalty, and interest levied.On Thursday, the shares of Vodafone Idea closed 8% higher at Rs 11.62 on the BSE.Also read | Emkay projects 44% downside for Vodafone Idea shares despite Rs 87,695 crore AGR relief. items.snippet: Vodafone Idea shares are likely to stay in focus after the company received a CGST order confirming a tax demand, including penalty and interest. The telecom operator has disputed the order and plans to take legal action, stating that the potential financial impact could extend to the full amount demanded by the tax authorities.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea receives Rs 638 crore GST penalty order; co says it will take legal action
items.body: Vodafone Idea has received a penalty order of Rs 637.91 crore from the Office of the Additional Commissioner, Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST), Ahmedabad South, according to a regulatory filing released by the company on Thursday.The order has been passed under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, confirming a penalty of Rs 6,37,90,68,254 along with the demand of tax and applicable interest, the company said. Vodafone Idea said it received the order on December 31, 2025.According to the filing, the action relates to allegations of short payment of tax and excess availment of input tax credit. The maximum financial impact on the company would be to the extent of the tax demand, interest and penalty levied under the order. However, the telecom operator said it does not agree with the order and will take appropriate legal action against it.Centre relief on AGR duesCentre has extended significant relief to Vodafone Idea by freezing the telecom operator’s outstanding adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues and approving a five-year moratorium on payments.The Cabinet-approved relief package, which confirms an earlier Economic Times report dated December 15, provides for the freezing of Vodafone Idea’s statutory dues at ₹87,695 crore as on December 31. However, the company told stock exchanges that it has not received any formal communication from the government on the proposed relief.Responding to exchange queries, Vodafone Idea said: “We have not received any communication from the government in relation to the above reported matter. As and when there is any development which requires disclosure, we will do the needful.”Officials familiar with the matter previously told ET that the frozen dues would be repaid over a 10-year period, from FY 2031-32 to FY 2040-41. The dues will also be reassessed by the Department of Telecommunications based on deduction verification guidelines and audit reports, a process that could potentially lower the final payable amount.However, AGR liabilities relating to FY 2017-18 and FY 2018-19 will continue to be payable by Vodafone Idea over the next five years, from FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31, the report said.The government is expected to formally convey the relief details to Vodafone Idea through an official communication in the coming days.SC verdict on Vi's fateThe AGR dispute stems from a Supreme Court ruling in October 2019, which upheld the government’s definition of adjusted gross revenue and covered dues up to FY 2016-17. Subsequently, the Department of Telecommunications calculated additional dues for FY 2017-18 and FY 2018-19 and raised demands on telecom operators, including Vodafone Idea and Bharti Airtel.In September 2021, the government granted a four-year moratorium on AGR dues up to FY 2018-19, which expires in the current financial year. Under the latest relief framework, Vodafone Idea has been granted an additional five-year moratorium for AGR dues up to FY 2016-17, while dues for FY 2017-18 and FY 2018-19 remain payable.Separately, the government had earlier approved conversion of AGR dues into equity, following which it now holds a 49 per cent stake in Vodafone Idea. The Aditya Birla Group and Vodafone Group Plc hold 9.50 per cent and 16.07 per cent stakes, respectively.The relief applies only to Vodafone Idea, while Bharti Airtel continues to service its statutory dues as scheduled, the report said. Government officials cited in the report said the measures were aimed at preserving competition in a highly concentrated telecom sector and safeguarding consumer interests.Vodafone Idea has been under sustained financial stress, losing market share to rivals Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio, and lagging in 5G rollout due to funding constraints. The relief follows Supreme Court orders dated November 3 and December 27, 2025, which allowed the government to revisit the issue in view of public interest, the government’s substantial stake in the company, and the interests of around 20 crore subscribers.The resolution of the AGR issue could improve Vodafone Idea’s ability to raise fresh capital, including its proposed fundraise of ₹25,000 crore.
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea faces a Rs 637.91 crore penalty from CGST Ahmedabad South. The government has provided significant relief by freezing AGR dues and approving a five-year payment moratorium. This move aims to support the telecom operator amidst financial stress and ensure competition in the sector. The company awaits formal communication on these developments.

items.headline: Emkay projects 44% downside for Vodafone Idea shares despite Rs 87,695 crore AGR relief. Here’s why
items.body: The Union Cabinet’s decision to approve a relief package for Vodafone Idea (VI) that freezes a substantial portion of its adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues, offering near-term cash-flow relief, falls short of the waiver that markets were anticipating, Emkay Global said in a note.The brokerage, which has a sell rating and a target price of Rs 6, implies a downside potential of over 44%. It indicated that the Cabinet has granted the company a five-year, interest-free moratorium on AGR dues pertaining to periods prior to FY18. These dues, amounting to Rs 87,695 crore, will now be repaid over a 10-year period from FY32 to FY41. However, AGR liabilities related to FY18 and FY19 will remain unchanged and will be payable as scheduled over FY26 to FY31.The decision dashed expectations of a meaningful haircut on AGR liabilities. “Contrary to the street’s expectations of at least a 50% waiver, no waiver on the pending dues linked to AGR was provided by the Cabinet,” Emkay noted, adding that the absence of a write-off limits the upside from the relief package.As part of the decision, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) will set up a committee within six to eight months to reassess the AGR dues. This exercise will include a recalculation and reevaluation of AGR liabilities, including a review of interest and penalty components, and a reassessment of the frozen dues based on audit reports. Emkay pointed out that this leaves some scope for a further reduction in the AGR liability, although the outcome and timing remain uncertain.The report also highlighted that the DoT has raised an additional AGR demand of Rs 9,450 crore linked to reassessment and reconciliation for the FY16–17 period. Under the earlier payment schedule as of March 2025, Vodafone Idea was required to pay Rs 75,900 crore in six equal annual instalments starting March 2026. The revised framework pushes out a significant portion of these payments, easing near-term pressure on cash flows.Despite this relief, Emkay cautioned that Vodafone Idea’s financial position remains highly stressed. While the AGR package addresses one part of the problem, the company continues to face deferred spectrum payment obligations of nearly Rs 1.2 lakh crore, with significant repayments scheduled between FY26 and FY44.Operationally, the numbers offer little comfort. VI’s pre-Ind AS 116 annualised EBITDA stands at just Rs 898 crore, equivalent to 6.7% of its spectrum debt. Cash balance was Rs 3,080 crore as of the end of Q2 FY26. Management has guided for capital expenditure of Rs 7,500–8,000 crore in FY26, which Emkay said further exacerbates leverage pressures. “Current EBITDA is insufficient to meet the capex or the spectrum debt repayment requirement,” the brokerage said.Even after excluding AGR dues, leverage remains elevated, prompting Emkay to argue that the government will need to consider a broader plan to address spectrum liabilities. The report said further capital infusion and restructuring of spectrum debt are critical for the company’s long-term sustainability.On the outlook, Emkay acknowledged that repeated government interventions suggest an intent to keep Vodafone Idea solvent. However, it added that deeper reforms are required to make the company structurally stronger with manageable leverage.Valuations, too, remain a concern. The stock is trading at 13.6 times FY27E EV/EBITDA, which Emkay considers expensive in light of high leverage and limited visibility on the government’s stance on spectrum debt.Also read: January jinx weighs for Nifty bulls: 80% failure rate in last 10 years linked to FII selling(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times.)
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea receives a five-year moratorium on AGR dues, easing near-term cash flow but leaving high leverage and spectrum obligations a major concern.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea shares jump 10% as Rs 5,836 crore group settlement lifts survival hopes
items.body: Shares of Vodafone Idea, one of India’s most beleaguered telecom operators, climbed as much as 9.9% to a high of Rs 11.83 on the BSE on Thursday, after disclosures showed the company will receive about Rs 5,836 crore from its promoter Vodafone Group as part of a reworked settlement of legacy liability claims.The payment stems from an amendment to the Contingent Liability Adjustment Mechanism, or CLAM, agreed at the time of the 2017 merger between Vodafone India and Idea Cellular. Under the revised terms of the implementation agreement, Vodafone Group promoters will release Rs 2,307 crore to Vodafone Idea over the next 12 months, according to regulatory filings by both companies.In addition, Vodafone Group has earmarked its entire holding of 328 crore shares in Vodafone Idea for the benefit of the Indian operator. Vodafone Idea will have the right to instruct Vodafone to sell these shares in one or more tranches, with any cash proceeds transferred to the company. As of the date of the amendment agreement, the market value of the earmarked shares stood at Rs 3,529 crore, Vodafone Idea said in its filing.CLAM pact revised ahead of deadlineThe CLAM framework was designed to cover pre-merger contingent liabilities related to legal, regulatory, tax and other matters of the two merging entities. Vodafone’s maximum exposure under the mechanism was capped at Rs 8,369 crore at the time of the merger and, after payments already made, the reduced exposure was capped at Rs 6,394 crore. Following an extension, the deadline for the pact was December 31, 2025.Consequent to the amended terms of the implementation agreement, Vodafone Idea said a sum of approximately Rs 5,836 crore is now receivable by the company.AGR relief adds to momentumThe rally in Vodafone Idea shares also came against the backdrop of a PTI report saying the Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a major relief package for the telecom operator, including freezing its outstanding adjusted gross revenue, or AGR, dues and granting a five-year moratorium on payments.According to the report, the measures aim to protect government interests, given the Centre holds about a 48.9% stake in Vodafone Idea, while ensuring competition in the telecom sector and safeguarding the interests of the company’s roughly 20 crore consumers.The Cabinet, headed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, agreed to freeze Vodafone Idea’s AGR dues at Rs 87,695 crore, with payments to begin in the 2031-32 fiscal year and extend through 2040-41, the PTI report said. The frozen dues will be reassessed by the Department of Telecommunications based on deduction-verification guidelines issued in 2020 and audit reports, with a government-appointed committee determining the final payable amount, which will be binding on both sides.AGR dues are statutory payments owed by telecom companies to the government based on adjusted gross revenue, the base on which licence fees and spectrum usage charges are calculated. As part of the relief package, AGR dues for FY 2017-18 and FY 2018-19, finalised under a Supreme Court order in September 2020, will be paid over FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31 without change. The PTI report pegged this at roughly Rs 120 crore a year, or between Rs 700 crore and Rs 800 crore over six years.Company seeks clarityResponding to a clarification sought by BSE, Vodafone Idea said after market hours on Wednesday: “We have not received any communication from the government in relation to the above-reported matter. As and when there is any development which requires disclosure, we will do the needful.”Government sources cited by PTI said the move was taken in public interest and to avoid excessive concentration in the telecom sector.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of the Economic Times)
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea shares jumped nearly 10% after regulatory filings showed the telecom operator will receive Rs 5,836 crore from Vodafone Group under a revised liability settlement, while separate reports pointed to fresh government relief on its adjusted gross revenue dues, together offering a rare boost to the debt-laden telco.

items.headline: Sudeep Bandyopadhyay on Voda Idea: Relief eases stress, execution is the real test
items.body: Shares of Vodafone Idea witnessed sharp volatility after an initial spike gave way to a steep decline, leaving investors puzzled about the finer details of the government relief package. The stock had jumped nearly 6% when the news first broke but later slipped around 7%, reflecting uncertainty over what the announcement truly means for the company’s balance sheet and future funding ability.On ET Now, the sharp reversal was flagged as a sign that the market may be reading more than what meets the eye.Responding to this, Market Expert, Sudip Bandyopadhyay said that while clarity will emerge only after a formal announcement or press conference, the relief appears constructive from Vodafone Idea’s perspective.“Well, we have to wait for the press conference or the formal announcement, but on the face of it this looks to be a very good development from the Vodafone Idea point of view. This relief and freezing the amount is a big relief and also giving this five-six years breather where they do not have to pay anything on this account. So, the payment starts from 32 and continues till 41. So, it is a very-very positive development from a Vodafone balance sheet point of view and the financial stress to a great extent gets reduced undoubtedly.”He added that while financial pressure eases, operational challenges remain a key concern for the company.“Of course, Vodafone has an operational challenge as well. Customers continuously and that needs to be plugged sooner the better and I am sure Vodafone will be able to focus on the operational aspects much more now to take forward the company and from a consumer perspective, the government is absolutely determined to prevent a duopoly and that is a good news.”However, the market’s disappointment appears to stem from expectations that the relief would go a step further. ET Now pointed out that the moratorium does not materially improve Vodafone Idea’s ability to raise fresh bank funding.“One of the reasons why the stock has fallen drastically is because it does not give the balance sheet enough leeway to borrow more from the banks. This debt remains on the balance sheet though this in the form of a moratorium and the payment has to come from 2032 to 2041. But the expectation was that there will be a waiver of penalty and interest, as a result of which the debt in the balance sheet will come down and they will be able to go to banks and financial institutions and borrow for their capex going forward, that is not going to happen now unless there is fresh strategic investment that comes into Vodafone and there is a headroom that opens up for bank borrowing.”Bandyopadhyay agreed that expectations had run ahead of reality, but stressed that the solution needs to be viewed in a broader policy context.“Yes, of course, what you say is right and expectations of all kind were being built in but considering everything I definitely feel that this is a positive development. Waving a significant amount is extremely difficult from government’s point of view as well because there will be multiple questions raised, other operators will also start clamouring for similar relief and the government definitely wanted to prevent that and that is the reason why this solution was worked out.”He noted that while the relief does not immediately improve borrowing capacity, it gives the company valuable breathing room.“Yes, from a balance sheet perspective this incremental borrowing capacity, etc, does not get created but it is a very good relief. Five years they do not have to bother about this amount and after that once the performance hopefully has improved, profitability has been restored in a big way, they will have to start paying and they will pay this over a 10-year period.”Calling the market reaction excessive, he suggested sentiment could shift once investors reassess the longer-term impact.“So, maybe market is overreacting, but it is a positive development and I am sure at some stage the market will start factoring in that. Of course, the operational issues which I mentioned earlier remains and that needs to be addressed without any further delay.”For now, Vodafone Idea’s stock movement reflects the tension between immediate balance-sheet relief and the absence of a clean slate on debt—leaving investors divided on whether the government’s support is a turning point or just a temporary pause in the company’s long-running struggle.
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea shares experienced sharp volatility following a government relief package. While the announcement provided a significant financial breather by deferring payments, it failed to address concerns about the company's ability to secure fresh bank funding, leading to investor disappointment and a stock decline.

items.headline: Voda Idea shares jump 4% as Vodafone Group commits Rs 5,836 crore support
items.body: Vodafone Idea shares rose as much as 4% to an intraday high of Rs 11.18 on Thursday, January 1, 2026, after the company announced it would receive Rs 5,836 crore from its promoter group, Vodafone Group, following an amendment to the long-standing Implementation Agreement related to contingent liabilities arising from the Vodafone–Idea merger.Under the revised agreement, Vodafone Group Promoters will release Rs 2,307 crore over the next 12 months, while the remaining amount will be secured through a share-based mechanism.The amended IA pertains to the Contingent Liability Adjustment Mechanism (CLAM), under which Vodafone Idea had earlier recognised Rs 8,369 crore as receivable from promoters. After accounting for Rs 1,975 crore already received, the balance CLAM amount stood at Rs 6,394 crore. As per the revised terms, around Rs 5,836 crore is now recoverable by the company.Sensex, Nifty today: Catch all the LIVE stock market action hereAs part of the recovery structure, certain Vodafone Group shareholders have earmarked 3.28 billion equity shares of Vodafone Idea for a period of five years. Proceeds from the sale of these shares, executed at the company’s direction, will accrue to Vodafone Idea. The market value of the earmarked shares is estimated at Rs 3,529 crore, based on the NSE closing price of Rs 10.76 per share as of the amendment date.The amendment agreement was executed on December 31, 2025, extending the earlier sunset clause and providing greater clarity on the settlement of legacy contingent liabilities. The company clarified that receipt of the CLAM amount is not linked to any pre-condition payments to the Department of Telecommunications.The transaction is a modification to an existing related-party arrangement with promoter group entities and does not involve any issuance of shares, loans, or special rights.On Wednesday, Vodafone Idea shares dropped 10.85%, closing at ₹10.76 on the BSE. During the day, the stock briefly hit a 52-week high of ₹12.80 before slipping back to its closing level. The company currently has a market capitalization of ₹1,16,577 crore.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
items.snippet: Vodafone Idea shares surged after its promoter group, Vodafone Group, agreed to inject Rs 5,836 crore. This follows a revised agreement on contingent liabilities, with a portion paid upfront and the rest secured via a share-based mechanism. The deal aims to settle legacy issues, boosting investor confidence and the company's financial standing.
